papers.abstract: The complex interactions between tumors and microbes within the tumor-microbe microenvironment (TMME) are increasingly recognized as critical determinants of tumor progression and therapeutic response. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the presence of intratumoral microbes (ITMs), their routes of entry into tumors, and their functional roles within the TMME, and highlights emerging TMME-targeted strategies for diagnosis and treatment of tumors with ITMs. ITMs can profoundly influence tumor biology by modulating cellular signaling and immune responses, with consequent changes in therapeutic efficacy. For instance, Fusobacterium nucleatum impairs CD8+ T-cell infiltration via succinic acid in drug-resistant colorectal cancer, while cytidine deaminase-expressing bacteria inactivate gemcitabine in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. We summarize the defining characteristics of the TMME, including hypoxia, acidity, and oxidative stress, as well as microbial-associated features such as biofilm formation, bacterial enzymes, and metabolite production. These factors collectively contribute to a dynamic ecosystem that supports microbial persistence and impacts tumor development, immune regulation, and treatment outcomes. Current therapeutic strategies targeting ITM tumors are critically evaluated, including microbial modulation approaches, non-antibiotic modalities, and nanomedicine-based co-delivery systems that combine antibiotics with chemotherapeutics. Co-delivery systems, such as a liposome platform that delivers ciprofloxacin and gemcitabine, allow simultaneous targeting of tumor cells and intratumoral microbes by exploiting the acidic, hypoxic, and enzyme- and metabolite-rich features of the TMME. This TMME-responsive design allows site-specific drug release while eliminating ITMs, and thereby overcomes microbe-induced chemoresistance and enhances therapeutic efficacy. Finally, we highlight the opportunities and challenges associated with TMME-targeted interventions. While modulation or elimination of tumor-associated microbes represents a promising strategy for improving treatment outcomes, significant barriers remain, including a lack of standardized diagnostic tools, microbial heterogeneity, safety concerns, and limited mechanistic understanding of tumor-microbe interactions. Advances in this field will require integrated multi-omics approaches and better translational models for the development of precise, personalized therapies for ITM tumors.

papers.abstract: Retinoblastoma (RB) is the most common childhood intraocular malignancy. RB1 germline variants predispose to early-onset bilateral disease, but associations with treatment response and post-treatment ocular outcomes are incompletely characterized. Retrospective cohort study of 120 intraocular RB patients treated at Children's Hospital Affiliated to Shandong University (2016-2021). Patients were stratified into carriers (n = 41; pathogenic/likely pathogenic RB1 germline variants) and non-carriers (n = 79). Eye-level generalized estimating equations (GEE) evaluated treatment response and post-treatment outcomes, adjusting for International Intraocular Retinoblastoma Classification (IIRC) stage, laterality, age, sex, and five separately entered treatment modalities (intravenous, intra-arterial, and intravitreal chemotherapy; laser photocoagulation; cryotherapy). Carriers presented younger, with more bilateral disease and multifocal disease. At the eye level, non-carrier eyes showed higher proportions of IIRC Group D/E (83.3% vs. 55.2%, p < 0.001) and mixed growth pattern (41.7% vs. 16.4%, p = 0.001), while carrier eyes had a higher proportion of endophytic pattern (71.6% vs. 54.8%, p = 0.043). On eye-level GEE analysis, RB1 variant status was associated with post-treatment cataract (adjusted OR = 3.42, 95% CI 1.13-10.30, p = 0.029). Post-treatment phthisis bulbi occurred exclusively in carrier eyes (4/67 vs. 0/84, p = 0.037). At the eye level, RB1 variant status was associated with distinct IIRC stage distribution and growth patterns, and with post-treatment cataract after adjusting for five separately entered treatment modalities-though this cataract finding should be considered hypothesis-generating given the absence of detailed treatment dose data. These findings suggest a potential role for RB1 pathway dysfunction in ocular tissue vulnerability beyond tumor suppression, warranting prospective validation.

papers.abstract: The incidence, risk factors and clinical implications of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in patients with glioblastoma have not been well studied. We identified patients with WHO 2021 glioblastoma in the Zurich database and explored the incidence, putative risk factors, management and outcome of ICH. ICH was verified by central MRI and imaging report review. Among 387 patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2019, 40 had an ICH at diagnosis. Of these, 4 patients were on anti-platelet agents, and 2 patients were on anticoagulation. All ICH occurred in the tumor region. Patients with ICH at diagnosis were younger (p = 0.001), had less cardiac disease (p = 0.027), and had larger tumors (p = 0.020). Median survival was similar between patients with (15 months) or without (13 months) ICH at diagnosis. Among 22 patients with ICH later in the disease course, 7 patients (37%) experienced ICH prior to first progression. ICH were not intratumoral in 8 patients. Ten patients (45%) had no change in management, 7 patients (32%) were referred to palliative care. Nine patients (50%) had been pre-exposed to bevacizumab, yet, 193 patients (53%) without ICH had received bevacizumab, too. Five patients (23%) had platelet counts below 100,000/µl within 14 days prior to ICH. Median survival in the 22 patients who experienced ICH after diagnosis (17 months) was not inferior than in patients without ICH (13 months). ICH is rare in glioblastoma. It may be related to intrinsic features of the tumor and its blood vessels, however, platelet count and blood pressure should be monitored regularly. ICH does not signify a poor outcome overall.

papers.abstract: SPPADE symptoms (Sleep disturbance, Pain, Physical function impairment, Anxiety, Depression/distress, and Energy deficit/fatigue) may result from cancer and its treatment. The aim of this analysis was to characterize SPPADE symptoms in patients with stage 1-4 breast cancer. SPPADE data came from the Enhanced, EHR-facilitated Cancer Symptom Control (E2C2) study, a pragmatic cluster-randomized trial designed to evaluate a symptom management intervention in routine practice (Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03892967. Registered March 25, 2019). Symptom severity was measured on a 0-10 scale via an investigator-developed survey administered by patient portal, in-clinic tablet, or interactive voice response (phone) in association with an outpatient oncology encounter. Scores of 4-6 were categorized as "moderate" and ≥ 7 as "severe." In this analysis, only data from each patient's initial survey were included. A total of 9,209 patients with breast cancer completed an initial E2C2 survey between March 2019 and January 2023. The proportion with moderate or severe SPPADE symptoms was: 23% moderate and 10% severe for sleep disturbance; 17% moderate and 7% severe for pain; 19% moderate and 8% severe for anxiety; 16% moderate and 6% severe for emotional distress; 26% moderate and 12% severe for fatigue; and 21% moderate and 8% severe for impaired physical function. Younger age, non-White race, being unmarried, being unemployed or having a disability, and more education were associated with greater overall symptom burden. SPPADE symptoms are common in patients with breast cancer, especially in those who are young, non-White, unmarried, unemployed, and more educated. Routine implementation of symptom surveillance and management of these modifiable symptoms is warranted in breast oncology.

papers.abstract: Chordoma is a rare, locally aggressive tumor arising from notochordal remnants with limited effective systemic treatment options. Growing interest in immunotherapy has prompted investigation of the chordoma tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and the development of immunotherapeutic strategies targeting its molecular and cellular components. This review synthesizes the current literature on the immune landscape of chordoma and evaluates the clinical evidence and translational rationale for immunotherapeutic strategies in this disease. A PRISMA-compliant systematic search of the ClinicalTrials.gov registry was conducted using disease- and immunotherapy-specific search terms. Records were screened for trials explicitly enrolling chordoma patients and investigating immunotherapy, including immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), tumor-associated antigen vaccines, oncolytic platforms, and adoptive cellular therapies. Supplementary literature review identified additional trials not captured in the registry search. Thirty clinical trials evaluating immunotherapy in chordoma were identified. The chordoma TIME is spatially compartmentalized, with tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as the dominant infiltrating immune population and effector T cells physically excluded from the tumor parenchyma. A clinically relevant subset of tumors harbor inflamed transcriptional states and clonally enriched T cell receptor repertoires, consistent with antigen-driven immune activity that is suppressed rather than absent. ICI-based strategies, particularly PD-1 blockade, have demonstrated durable disease control in a meaningful subset of patients. Brachyury-directed vaccines have established immunogenicity but have not consistently translated to objective responses. Oncolytic virotherapy has produced isolated responses in early-phase trials, whereas NK cell-engaging antibody strategies and B7-H3-directed CAR-T cells remain preclinical. Chordoma is not immunologically inert, but its immune-excluded TIME, macrophage-dominant immunosuppressive milieu, and low tumor mutational burden present distinct barriers to conventional immunotherapy. Given chordoma's indolent biology, objective response rate may underestimate clinical benefit, whereas disease control rate and progression-free survival are most interpretable in randomized trials or in single-arm trials requiring documented progression at enrollment. Biomarker-driven patient selection integrating tumor genomics, spatial immune architecture, and checkpoint expression will be essential for advancing rational combination immunotherapy in this disease.

papers.abstract: Long-term outcomes after partial-breast irradiation (PBI) versus whole-breast irradiation (WBI) for early-stage breast cancer remain uncertain. We compared long-term oncological outcomes, late effects, and cosmesis. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and CINAHL from database inception to 9 March, 2026. Eligible studies were randomised controlled trials comparing PBI with WBI after breast-conserving surgery for stage 0-II breast cancer, with at least 7 years of follow-up. The primary outcome was ipsilateral breast tumour recurrence (IBTR). Secondary outcomes were non-breast cancer mortality (NBCM), overall, disease-free and breast cancer-specific survival, locoregional recurrence, contralateral breast cancer, late effects, and cosmesis. Random-effects models estimated hazard ratios (HRs); Peto odds ratios (ORs) were used for NBCM. The study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261334941). Twelve trials including 15,670 women were included. PBI was associated with higher IBTR overall (HR 1.61, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.08-2.41; p = 0.02; I2 = 71%). In the prespecified external-beam subgroup comprising three trials, the pooled HR was 1.24 (95% CI 0.89-1.73; p = 0.21; I2 = 0%), without a statistically significant difference. NBCM was lower overall with PBI (OR 0.77, 0.64-0.91; p = 0.003; I2 = 0%), but not in the external-beam subgroup (OR 0.73, 0.52-1.03; p = 0.07; I2 = 0%). Overall, disease-free, and breast cancer-specific survival were similar. Once-daily external-beam PBI and multicatheter brachytherapy showed favourable cosmesis and fewer late effects, whereas twice-daily 3D-conformal radiotherapy was associated with poorer cosmesis. PBI should not be considered a single treatment approach. Long-term oncological and cosmetic outcomes vary across PBI techniques and fractionation schedules, highlighting the importance of technique-specific evidence. The NBCM signal remains hypothesis-generating.

papers.abstract: Most genomic studies of adult-type diffuse gliomas have focused on predominantly European ancestry populations, limiting the generalizability of molecular classifications and precision medicine approaches. We assembled a multi-institutional glioma cohort of diverse patients to investigate how germline ancestry, molecular subtypes, and mutational processes shape tumor biology and clinical outcomes. We analyzed 1,102 adults with WHO 2021-classified diffuse gliomas (IDH-mutant, 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma; IDH-mutant astrocytoma; IDH-wildtype glioma) from seven U.S. institutions. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) of FFPE tumors identified somatic alterations and COSMIC SBS mutational signatures. Genetic ancestry was estimated from WES using 1000 Genomes reference populations. Overall survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and multivariable models. The cohort included 66.9% European (EUR), 21.1% Admixed American/Hispanic (AMR), 10.3% Admixed African (AFR), and 1.6% Asian (AS) ancestry. Survival followed expected molecular hierarchy (median overall survival: oligodendroglioma 15.7 years, astrocytoma 10.6 years, IDH-wildtype glioma 1.9 years). Within oligodendroglioma, AMR patients showed improved survival versus EUR (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.94; p = 0.011), with similar trends across subtypes. While somatic profiling confirmed canonical subtype-defining alterations, significant differences in the rates of genomic abnormalities like ATRX mutation spoke to potential compositional distinctions between ethnic groups for less common IDH-wildtype glioma variants. Mutational signature analysis identified subtype-specific signatures, including therapy-associated signatures. Chemotherapy-related signatures were more frequent in EUR and AMR than in AFR. This ancestrally diverse glioma cohort confirms established molecular classifications and identifies ancestry-associated differences in survival, somatic alterations, and mutational processes, indicating the need for broad representation to inform precision neuro-oncology.

papers.abstract: Cancer survivors face elevated cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, yet practical markers for identifying high-risk survivors are limited. The triglyceride‑glucose (TyG) index and its derivatives combining TyG with body mass index (TyG-BMI), waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR), or waist circumference (TyG-WC) have been validated in general populations, but their comparative performance and threshold effects in cancer survivors remain unexplored. We evaluated all four indices for incident CVD, coronary artery disease (CAD), stroke, and atrial fibrillation (AF), and identified risk thresholds. This prospective cohort study included 24,763 cancer survivors from the UK Biobank without pre‑existing CVD. All four indices were calculated at baseline. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for CVD as a composite of CAD, stroke, and AF, and for each component separately. Restricted cubic splines characterized nonlinear dose‑response relationships and threshold effects. Subgroup analyses were performed by cancer type and lifestyle factors. During a median 15.9‑year follow‑up, 4590 CVD events occurred. Per‑standard deviation increases in TyG, TyG‑BMI, TyG‑WHtR, and TyG‑WC were associated with 6% (HR 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.09), 14% (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.10-1.17), 14% (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.10-1.18), and 16% (HR 1.16, 95% CI 1.12-1.20) higher CVD risk, respectively. Associations with CAD were similar (per-SD HRs 1.14-1.21), with none for stroke. TyG‑BMI and TyG-WHtR showed nonlinear associations with CVD, with risk accelerating beyond inflection points of 261.54 and 5.59, respectively. Associations were strongest in breast, colorectal, and prostate cancers, whereas no association was observed in hematologic malignancies. For AF, the three obesity-combined indices were positively associated, whereas TyG alone exhibited a J‑shaped relationship. The obesity-combined indices, particularly those incorporating BMI and waist-to-height ratio, are independently associated with higher CVD and CAD risk. Thresholds of TyG‑BMI > 261.54 and TyG‑WHtR > 5.59 may help identify high‑risk survivors.

papers.abstract: To assess the quality and accuracy of common large language model chatbots in answering physician-level gynecologic oncology management questions. Three common chatbots (Microsoft CoPilot GPT 5.1, Chat GPT 5.0 Basic, and OpenEvidence 2026) were used. Twenty different gynecology oncology management questions were entered identically into each chatbot. Responses were blinded and randomly assigned and reviewed by attending physicians. They were assessed for accuracy and completeness (0 = not accurate or complete, 1 = accurate, 2 = accurate and complete). Each response was assessed for quality with the DISCERN instrument, and for understandability and actionability by patients, using the patient education materials assessment tool (PEMAT). Readability statistics were collected for each response to include: Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level Score, passive sentence percentage, and word count. Descriptive statistics and linear mixed-effects models were used to compare chatbot performance metrics. OpenEvidence was the most accurate and complete (1.45), followed by ChatGPT (1.22) and CoPilot (0.98, p = 0.028). OpenEvidence had the highest DISCERN score, followed by CoPilot and ChatGPT (50.7, 41.0, 40.08, p < 0.001). ChatGPT had the highest PEMAT score, followed by CoPilot and OpenEvidence (82.2%, 81.3%, 66.5%, p < 0.001). Reading ease was highest with CoPilot (16.6, p < 0.001). OpenEvidence had the highest Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level score (17.9, p < 0.001). With a one-way ANOVA comparison by question type, there was no significant difference in accuracy between the chatbot responses. For use by gynecologic oncologists, OpenEvidence was the most accurate and complete chatbot. Further studies are needed to continue to evaluate large language models as they improve and integrate into clinical practices.

papers.abstract: This study evaluated the prognostic value of molecular classification in atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH) or early endometrioid endometrial carcinoma (EC) patients receiving fertility-sparing treatment (FST). We retrospectively analyzed 552 FST recipients stratified by molecular subtypes. 552 patients (EC = 244, AEH = 308) were classified into NSMP (n = 496), MMRd (n = 29), POLEmut (n = 15), and p53abn (n = 12). All underwent hysteroscopic intervention plus hormonal therapy. Baseline characteristics, complete response (CR), and recurrence were compared across subtypes. Efficacy was assessed via hysteroscopy every 3 months. Baseline metabolic/hormonal parameters were comparable across subtypes. In AEH, age (P = 0.001), LH (P = 0.042), and parity (P = 0.046) differed significantly. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed POLEmut had shorter relapse-free survival (RFS) than NSMP (P = 0.023), and p53abn had inferior RFS versus NSMP (P = 0.010). In EC (NSMP), multivariate Cox regression identified GnRH-a plus letrozole as independently associated with improved CR (HR = 2.860, P < 0.001), while dydrogesterone maintenance predicted recurrence (HR = 7.943, P = 0.003). In AEH (NSMP), univariate analysis showed LNG-IUS was the sole predictor of favorable CR (HR = 1.935, 95% CI:1.398-2.678, P < 0.001), whereas dydrogesterone maintenance increased recurrence risk versus LNG-IUS (HR = 2.694, P = 0.041). Molecular classification holds clinical promise in EC/AEH undergoing FST. RFS varied significantly across subtypes, with POLEmut and p53abn showing worse outcomes. In NSMP, GnRH-a + letrozole improved CR in EC, while LNG-IUS improved CR in AEH; dydrogesterone maintenance was associated with higher recurrence risk than LNG-IUS in this subtype.

papers.abstract: Clinical and prognostic differences between never-smokers and ever-smokers with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) remain incompletely characterized. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study to compare clinical characteristics and survival outcomes between never-smokers and ever-smokers with SCLC, evaluate potential indirect pathways linking smoking history with overall survival (OS), and explore treatment-associated survival patterns. A total of 1153 patients from three tertiary hospitals in China were included, comprising 340 never-smokers and 813 ever-smokers. Ever-smoking was associated with worse OS in univariable analysis (HR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.04-1.38; p = 0.013), but this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (HR = 1.04, 95% CI: 0.82-1.32; p = 0.729). In separate single-mediator analyses, indirect effects were observed through surgical resection and clinical stage, with estimated mediated proportions of 39.9% and 16.1%, respectively; these estimates were derived from separate models and are not additive. Exploratory analyses of recorded treatment history showed chemotherapy-associated lower mortality hazards in both smoking groups, while ever-smoking was associated with poorer OS among patients with recorded radiotherapy exposure. Because exact treatment timing was unavailable, these treatment-related findings should be interpreted as exploratory associations rather than causal treatment effects. Smoking history was associated with distinct clinical characteristics but was not independently associated with survival after multivariable adjustment. These findings support further prospective investigation of smoking-associated clinical heterogeneity in SCLC.

papers.abstract: Tumour-resident bacteria are increasingly recognised as modulators of colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and therapy resistance, with prior studies typically focussing on relative abundance of specific bacteria. However, the landscape of total bacterial burden in CRC is poorly understood. We performed a comprehensive analysis of bacterial load in 595 CRC tumours. The association with MSI-H status was validated in an independent cohort of 160 CRC tumours using in situ hybridisation and ex vivo adhesion assays. Bacterial load was not associated with patient demographics or tumour stage, but it was associated with molecular classifications of CRC including microsatellite instability (MSI), chromosomal instability, CpG island methylator phenotype, and consensus molecular subtypes, with only increased bacteria in MSI-H tumours remaining independently significant upon multivariable analyses. TP53 and APC mutant tumours exhibited decreased bacterial load in MSS tumours. At both the gene and protein level, high bacterial load was associated with increased inflammatory signalling. Further analysis of systems-level metabolic rewiring suggests elevated glycan metabolism in high bacteria tumours. Using 160 patient tumours, we confirmed that bacterial load was positively independently associated with both MSI-H status and levels of the glycan Gal-GalNAc. Ex vivo adhesion assays indicate that the bacteria are preferentially adherent to MSI-H tumours, and that bacteria adhesion to tumours is correlated with baseline microbial abundance. MSI-H tumours have elevated bacteria burden, and elevated bacterial burden is associated with specific mutations, transcriptional profiles, and metabolic landscapes across CRC tumours. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive landscape of how bacterial load is associated with clinicopathological and molecular alterations. NIH, VeloSano, ACS.

papers.abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) has poor outcomes in intermediate- to high-risk disease, and the role of PD-1 blockade with frontline neoadjuvant chemotherapy is unknown. This ongoing multicenter, open-label phase 1/2 trial evaluates neoadjuvant pucotenlimab plus risk-stratified chemotherapy. The primary endpoints are safety and pathologic response rate (pCR/mPR). Among the 42 enrolled patients (median follow-up, 13 months), no dose-limiting toxicities are observed, with no treatment-related discontinuation or death. Thirty-nine patients are efficacy evaluable, with an objective response rate (ORR) of 74.4% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 57.9%-87.0%), a pCR/mPR rate of 56.0% (95% CI: 34.9%-75.6%), and marked heterogeneity across subtypes (78.6% in embryonal RMS [ERMS] vs. 33.3% in alveolar RMS [ARMS]). At the early on-treatment assessment, plasma circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is undetectable in 6/6 (100%) patients with pCR/mPR and 3/6 (50%) patients with non-MPR, whereas persistent ctDNA is observed primarily in patients with high baseline ctDNA concentrations. These interim findings show encouraging activity with manageable toxicity.

papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is highly aggressive and associated with poor prognosis, highlighting the need for safe and effective targeted therapies. Analyses of specimens and clinical data from patients with TNBC demonstrate that acylglycerol kinase (AGK) expression correlates with TNBC progression, supporting AGK as a potential therapeutic target. We identify P13, a flavonoid-derived small molecule that selectively targets AGK and covalently binds to its Cys72 residue. P13 inhibits AGK kinase-dependent activity involved in phosphatidic acid (PA) and lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) synthesis and its kinase-independent function in TIM22 complex formation. P13 induces mitochondrial dysfunction in TNBC cells, leading to inhibition of tumor cell proliferation and suppression of stemness. P13 exhibits favorable pharmacokinetic properties, oral bioavailability, and tolerability. In PDX models, P13 inhibits TNBC tumor growth as monotherapy and in combination with paclitaxel. These findings support AGK as a potential therapeutic target and provide a rationale for AGK-targeting strategies in TNBC.

papers.abstract: Fused in sarcoma (FUS) forms dynamic biomolecular condensates through phase separation, a process associated with stress responses and neurodegenerative diseases. Here, we use in-cell NMR spectroscopy to directly observe condensate formation of the FUS low-complexity (LC) domain in living cells. We identify a two-step process: initial droplet formation followed by time-dependent maturation, characterized by reduced internal mobility. Deletion mutant analysis reveals that while initial condensate formation is driven by collective multivalent interactions, the reversible amyloid core (RAC) region is essential for the subsequent maturation. Intracellular droplets form at concentrations well below the in vitro threshold, which cannot be explained by macromolecular crowding alone. Notably, droplet formation is suppressed under nutrient starvation, suggesting that ATP-dependent cellular activities indirectly promote FUS condensation. These findings demonstrate that the metabolically active intracellular environment modulates FUS condensate behavior, providing mechanistic insights into early events in pathological aggregation and establishing a general framework for studying condensates in cells.

papers.abstract: Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

papers.abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease.

papers.abstract: Pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) is a rare bone marrow failure characterized by the absence of erythroid precursor cells. While its autoimmune mechanisms are suspected, the genetic background remains unclear. To identify novel characteristic genetic abnormalities, we performed a comprehensive analysis of copy number alterations (CNAs) in 35 PRCA cases using CytoScan 750 K. The median number of CNAs per case was 27 (range, 1-59), involving a total of 16,853 genes. Notably, we discovered that the TARP gene (7p14.1) was deleted in 27 cases (77.1%), representing a higher frequency compared to 100 non-PRCA controls (q = 0.00234 after Benjamini-Hochberg [BH] correction; odds ratio, 9.13; 95% CI, 3.69-22.54). Using nail DNA, we confirmed that this TARP deletion was a somatic event. Furthermore, quantitative PCR demonstrated that the relative copy number of TARP was significantly lower in peripheral blood CD3-positive T-cells (0.518) than in CD3-negative cells (p = 0.000612 after Bonferroni correction). Clinical evaluations revealed that peripheral blood lymphocyte counts were significantly increased in PRCA cases with the TARP deletion (q = 0.0220 after BH correction). In conclusion, we demonstrate that TARP deletion is a frequent somatic abnormality localized to the T-cell fraction, suggesting a potential association with lymphocytosis in PRCA.

papers.abstract: ChemoHormonal Therapy Versus Androgen Ablation Randomized Trial for Extensive Disease in Prostate Cancer (CHAARTED) risk stratification is an important risk stratification tool in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC). However, clinicians are increasingly using prostate-specific membrane antigen-positron emission tomography (PSMA-PET)/computed tomography (CT). Here, the prognostic value of PSMA-total tumor volume (PSMA-TTV) for overall survival (OS) in a developmental cohort from the Enzalutamide in First-Line Androgen Deprivation Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer (ENZAMET) trial with validation in the larger Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardized Evaluation (PROMISE) Registry was evaluated. Participants who underwent PSMA-PET/CT before enrolment in the prospective phase 3 ENZAMET trial (development cohort) or were classified as having mHSPC in the ongoing international PROMISE Registry (validation cohort) were included, and PSMA-TTV was derived using a semiautomated method. In the ENZAMET dataset, the association of PSMA-TTV categories with time to progression and OS in addition to CHAARTED groups by conventional imaging, was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and log-rank tests. ENZAMET-derived PSMA-TTV categories were tested in the PROMISE mHSPC cohort using Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and log-rank tests and Cox regression analyses. Overall, 100 patients from ENZAMET and 993 patients from the PROMISE Registry were analyzed. The upper ENZAMET-derived PSMA-TTV category was ≥72 ml. In patients with CHAARTED criteria low-volume disease, 5-yr OS for PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml versus <72 ml was 36% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 16-83) versus 71% (60-85; p = 0.019) in survival curves; 5-yr OS for PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml was not associated with shorter OS in the ENZAMET subgroup (50% [32-78] vs 73% [63-85]; p = 0.063) but in the PROMISE mHSPC subgroup (33% [27-40] vs 78% [75-81]; p < 0.001). The hazard ratio for upper PSMA-TTV category ≥72 ml was 6.8 (95% CI = 5.3-8.7) in the PROMISE mHSPC subgroup. PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml from an ENZAMET cohort is prognostic for OS in the PROMISE mHSPC cohort. Further validation of PSMA-TTV as a prognostic biomarker with potential to be a predictive marker to identify patients for intensification is warranted.

papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and a subset of patients are refractory to or relapse after standard R-CHOP therapy. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death characterized by lipid peroxide accumulation. Although SLC7A11 is a key suppressor of ferroptosis, the post-translational mechanisms regulating SLC7A11 stability in DLBCL remain incompletely understood. Although OTUB1-mediated stabilization of SLC7A11 has been established in solid tumors, whether this post-translational axis operates in DLBCL - where ferroptosis sensitivity determines therapeutic response - remains unknown. We analyzed OTUB1 expression using public DLBCL datasets and validated its expression in DLBCL cell lines by qRT-PCR and western blotting. OTUB1 was silenced using siRNA or shRNA, and the effects on cell viability, lipid, ROS and glutathione levels, and cell death were assessed. Ferroptosis involvement was evaluated using ferrostatin-1 and Z-VAD-FMK. The interaction between OTUB1 and SLC7A11 was examined using co-immunoprecipitation, ubiquitination assays, and MG132-mediated proteasome inhibition. SLC7A11 rescue experiments were performed for mechanistic evaluation, and a nude-mouse xenograft model was used for in vivo validation. OTUB1 mRNA and protein levels are significantly increased in DLBCL tissues as compared to normal B cells. Knocking down OTUB1 in DLBCL cells decreased the metabolic activity, resulting in elevated lipid ROS levels and severe glutathione (GSH) depletion. The ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 effectively rescued the cells, whereas no significant effect was observed with the apoptosis blocker Z-VAD, suggesting that OTUB1 knockdown induced cell death via ferroptosis. Co-immunoprecipitation assay revealed a direct interaction between endogenous OTUB1 and SLC7A11. OTUB1 knockdown increased SLC7A11 ubiquitination and reduced SLC7A11 protein levels without significantly altering SLC7A11 mRNA expression, which suggested post-translational regulation. Ectopic expression of SLC7A11 in the OTUB1-depleted cells partially or substantially rescued cell viability, reduced accumulation of lipid ROS, and restored intracellular GSH levels. Finally, OTUB1 knockdown suppressed the growth of DLBCL tumor xenografts in vivo, which was accompanied by reduced SLC7A11 and Ki-67 expression in the tumor tissues. OTUB1 contributes to ferroptosis resistance in DLBCL cells by stabilizing SLC7A11. The OTUB1/SLC7A11 axis may represent a potential target for sensitizing DLBCL cells to ferroptotic cell death, although further clinical validation and pharmacological studies are required.

papers.abstract: Intraperitoneal treatments cause peritoneal sclerosis, which may be detrimental to quality-of-life. No method exists for an objective assessment of peritoneal sclerosis. Here, we develop a quantitative method for measuring the severity of peritoneal sclerosis, namely the Peritoneal Sclerosis Index (PSI). Laparoscopic videos of patients undergoing pressurized intraperitoneal aerosolized chemotherapy (PIPAC) at an NCI-designated cancer center were retrospectively analyzed. All videos were de-identified and scored by experienced surgical oncologists who were blinded to any patient characteristics. PSI scoring ranged from 0 to 39 and inter-rater reliability was assessed using intra-class coefficient (ICC). ICC estimates were calculated for both single-rater reliability (individual rater reliability) and the mean rating (two or more rater's reliability). PSI reliability was compared with that of the Peritoneal Carcinomatosis Index (PCI) in the same patient cohort. Normalized pairwise disagreement was explored to delineate regions of highest disagreement. A total of 28 laparoscopic patient videos from 15 patients (median age 61 years; 53% female; primary cancer: 5 appendix, 5 colorectal, and 5 biliary tract) undergoing PIPAC were evaluated by six surgeons. Overall inter-rater reliability was high, with a single-rater ICC of 0.87 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.78-0.93). Reliability improved with increasing numbers of raters. ICC values were comparable to those observed for PCI (single ICC 0.91). PSI reliability was maintained after PIPAC (single ICC 0.89). Pairwise analysis demonstrated region-specific variability; the highest disagreement observed in the central compartment (0.30, 0.26-0.33) and lowest in visceral regions (0.18, 0.16-0.20). Agreement within clinically relevant thresholds increased with wider tolerance, from 35.7% at ± 3 points to 85.7% at ± 7 points, with minimal differences before and after PIPAC. PSI demonstrated excellent inter-rater reliability for peritoneal sclerosis and can be incorporated in clinical trials focused on intraperitoneal therapies. Future work should investigate correlation of PSI with quality-of-life metrics.

papers.abstract: RNF43 is best known for removing the Wnt-receptor complex from the cell surface, thereby maintaining Wnt-signaling at minimal essential levels. Recent studies reported that RNF43-mutant colorectal cancers carrying the common BRAFV600E mutation, respond more effectively to combined BRAF/EGFR inhibition. To determine whether RNF43 directly regulates EGFR or BRAF protein abundance, multiple pancreatic and colorectal cancer cell line models were generated in which RNF43 was knocked out, repaired, or stably overexpressed. Total and cell surface EGFR levels, as well as endogenous BRAF expression, were quantified. Across all models, no consistent evidence emerges that RNF43 modulates endogenous EGFR or BRAF levels. R-spondins likewise fail to alter EGFR levels or internalization. Notably, elevated EGFR expression observed in a subset of RNF43 knockout clones is induced by unintended CRISPR/Cas9 vector integration rather than the absence of RNF43 itself, highlighting a previously underappreciated artifact that can confound interpretations of EGFR regulation in genome edited lines. Overall, the data argue against a direct and general role for RNF43 in controlling EGFR or BRAF protein abundance, contradicting recent reports that propose degradation of these targets. Further studies are required to resolve these discrepancies and clarify the mechanistic basis underlying these conflicting observations.

papers.abstract: ARID1A is one of the most frequently altered chromatin-remodeling genes in endometriosis-associated ovarian cancers, particularly ovarian clear cell and endometrioid carcinomas. Although ARID1A loss is widely recognized as an early driver event, its translational relevance extends beyond histotype classification. This review discusses ARID1A deficiency as a context-dependent molecular vulnerability state linking chromatin deregulation, stemness-associated plasticity, replication stress, DNA repair dependence, and immune remodeling. Mechanistically, ARID1A loss can promote PRC2/EZH2-, PI3K/AKT-, and Hippo-YAP/TAZ-associated plasticity while increasing transcription-replication conflicts, R-loop accumulation, checkpoint reliance, and sensitivity to DNA damage response-targeting strategies. Replication-stress-associated genomic instability may further engage cGAS-STING-dependent innate immune signaling, although the proposed Hippo-STING-stemness coupling remains incompletely validated in ovarian cancer. Therapeutically, these mechanisms support rational combinations involving ATR or PARP inhibition, epigenetic therapies, stemness-directed interventions, and immunotherapy-oriented strategies. However, ARID1A status alone is unlikely to serve as a universal predictor of response. Instead, ARID1A should be interpreted within composite biomarker frameworks incorporating histotype, homologous recombination or replication-stress features, and immune context. This review outlines a translational framework for biomarker-guided therapeutic development in ARID1A-deficient ovarian cancer.

papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has transformed the treatment landscape for hematologic malignancies and is under active clinical investigation in solid tumors that are refractory to standard therapies. However, clinical translation in solid tumors remains constrained by intratumoral antigen heterogeneity, limited trafficking and persistence, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and the potential for on-target/off-tumor toxicity and systemic immune-related adverse events. The 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting reported multiple early-phase clinical updates involving autologous and allogeneic CAR-T products for solid tumors. In this focused correspondence, we summarize 12 ASCO 2026 clinical studies reporting extractable efficacy and/or safety outcomes for CAR-T therapy in solid tumors. The included studies encompassed glioblastoma (GBM), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), gastrointestinal cancers, small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC), non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and colorectal peritoneal metastases. The reported strategies included dual-antigen targeting, armored CAR constructs, logic-gated receptors, regional delivery, induced pluripotent stem cell-derived allogeneic products, and mRNA-electroporated autologous CAR-T cells. Across these small, non-randomized early-phase studies, preliminary antitumor activity was observed in selected tumor types and biomarker-defined populations. However, substantial heterogeneity in patient populations, CAR designs, routes of administration, response criteria, follow-up duration, and evaluable populations precludes direct cross-trial efficacy comparisons. Larger prospective studies with longer follow-up, standardized biomarker strategies, and comparative trial designs are needed to define the clinical role of CAR-T therapy in solid tumors.

papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive malignancy with limited therapies and frequent resistance. Sacituzumab govitecan (SG), a TROP-2-directed antibody-drug conjugate, improves survival in metastatic TNBC, yet determinants of response remain poorly defined. Using a biobank of patient-derived organoids (PDOs), we show that SG sensitivity in PDOs predicts patient outcomes. Multi-omics profiling of SG-resistant PDOs identifies a transcriptionally plastic epithelial subpopulation enriched for PI3K-AKT signaling and pro-survival programs, which persists after treatment and drives resistance. In preclinical models, pharmacological inhibition of PI3K with alpelisib resensitizes resistant tumors to SG, restoring treatment efficacy and prolonging survival. Our findings identify PI3K-AKT signaling as a mechanism of SG resistance in TNBC and provide a rationale for PI3K-targeted combination therapy to improve SG efficacy.

papers.abstract: Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment1,2. How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour-stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome.

papers.abstract: Patients with stage IV locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LA-NPC) remain at high risk of recurrence and distant metastasis despite intensity-modulated radiotherapy and concurrent cisplatin-based chemotherapy. Paclitaxel plus platinum (TP) has yielded encouraging activity. This randomized, open-label phase II trial evaluated whether concurrent TP could improve progression-free survival (PFS) compared with standard high-dose cisplatin (DDP) during chemoradiotherapy. Patients with stage IV LA-NPC were randomly assigned 1 : 1 to concurrent TP (paclitaxel plus cisplatin every 4 weeks for two cycles; planned cumulative concurrent cisplatin dose, 160 mg/m2) or DDP (cisplatin every 3 weeks for three cycles; planned cumulative concurrent cisplatin dose, 300 mg/m2) during chemoradiotherapy. The primary endpoint was 3-year PFS in the intention-to-treat population. Between February 2017 and September 2019, 184 patients were enrolled (92 patients per group). Median follow-up was 47.6 months. The 3-year PFS rates were 68.2% [95% confidence interval (CI) 58.6-77.8] with TP and 72.8% (95% CI 63.8-81.8) with DDP [stratified hazard ratio (HR) 1.16, 95% CI 0.71-1.90, Plog-rank = 0.56]. The stratified HR for overall survival (OS) was 0.38 (95% CI 0.13-1.09, P = 0.07). Given the limited number of deaths, no OS advantage of TP can be concluded. The cumulative incidence of locoregional relapse and distant metastasis did not differ between groups. The DDP group had higher rates of any-grade nausea, vomiting, anorexia, constipation, and thrombocytopenia (all P < 0.05), whereas grade 3-4 neutropenia was numerically higher with TP (22.0% versus 13.5%, P = 0.14). Late toxicities did not differ significantly (all P ≥ 0.12). With a lower planned cumulative concurrent cisplatin dose in the TP arm, TP did not demonstrate an improvement in PFS compared with standard DDP in concurrent chemoradiotherapy for stage IV LA-NPC. These findings do not support replacing standard DDP with this reduced-cisplatin TP schedule and do not exclude a potential benefit of adding paclitaxel to an equivalent-dose cisplatin backbone.

papers.abstract: Liquid biopsy assays, particularly analyses of cell-free DNA (cfDNA), are becoming increasingly important in the clinical management of cancer. Over the past decade, the development of refined techniques to extract and analyse cfDNA from various biological fluids has expanded its potential in oncology. In particular, fragmentomics, the analysis of cfDNA structure and fragmentation patterns, has emerged as a sensitive approach for cancer detection, localization and characterization. Nevertheless, scalable and widespread implementation of fragmentomics in the clinical setting remains challenging because it requires careful consideration of various confounding variables. In this Review, we introduce the mechanisms underlying cfDNA fragmentomics, summarize its application in preclinical and clinical cancer research, describe the common pitfalls in fragmentomics research and chart strategies to address them. Finally, we introduce fragmentomics reporting for analysis, methods and evaluation (FRAME), a framework for the transparent reporting of results from fragmentomics studies. Adoption of FRAME could increase the robustness and reproducibility of the evidence required to expand the use of fragmentomics in cancer research.

papers.abstract: Pediatric and adolescent osteosarcoma (OS) and Ewing's sarcoma (EWS) are highly aggressive malignancies associated with poor outcomes in the relapsed or metastatic setting, where survival rates remain below 20-30% despite intensive multimodal therapy. The transmembrane tyrosine-kinase receptor HER2 is expressed in a substantial proportion of OS and EWS; however, current HER2-directed antibody-based therapies show limited efficacy, likely due to the low antigen expression in these tumors. HER2 expression was evaluated by flow-cytometry on adult and pediatric tumor cell lines, as well as in biopsy tissues from pediatric sarcoma patients. We generated two third-generation CAR.HER2 constructs carrying ΔCD19 as both a tracking marker and safety switch to improve the safety profile. Retroviral vectors, (4D5)CAR.HER2 and (2C4)CAR.HER2, incorporate trastuzumab- or pertuzumab-derived single-chain variable fragments (scFvs), respectively, which linker was optimized through structural bioinformatic. These scFvs are coupled to the CD28 and 4-1BB costimulatory domains and the CD3ζ signaling domains, to promote robust T-cell activation and persistence. The antitumor activity of CAR.HER2 T-cells was assessed in vitro and in vivo against HER2 + OS and EWS tumors. HER2 expression was detected in 87% of tumor cell lines and in 38.5% of OS and 36.8% of EWS patient samples. Both CAR.HER2 T-cells exhibited strong CAR expression and comparable immunophenotypic profiles, following T-cell transduction. In 2D/3D in vitro models, CAR.HER2 T-cells showed potent cytotoxic activity against HER2-high OS and HER2-low EWS cells, including trastuzumab-deruxtecan (T-DXd)-resistant tumor cell lines. In in vivo models, both CAR.HER2 T-cells achieved complete regression in HER2-high OS xenografts, while in HER2-low EWS xenograft model only (4D5)CAR.HER2 T-cells induced full tumor eradication, whereas (2C4)CAR.HER2 T-cells delayed tumor progression without achieving full tumor elimination. Xenoreactivity associated with CAR.HER2 T-cell expansion was successfully controlled via ΔCD19 activation using an anti CD19/CD3 T-cell engager, enabling selective CAR T-cell depletion and toxicity resolution. Overall, (4D5)CAR.HER2 T-cells demonstrated superior antitumor activity, persistence, and functional fitness, achieving rapid tumor clearance in HER2-low pediatric sarcoma models. The integrated ΔCD19 safety switch induce a prompt CAR T-cell elimination. These findings support the clinical translation of high-affinity-(4D5)CAR.HER2 T-cells and suggest broader applicability of this design for targeting HER2-low tumors and overcoming resistance to HER2-immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Spatially variable genes (SVGs) are crucial for understanding spatial heterogeneity in spatial transcriptomics. Yet SVGs are challenging to align with established biological axes and lack straightforward mechanistic interpretation, thereby limiting their ability to inform downstream experiments or clinical applications. Here, we introduce the concept of directionally variable genes (DVGs) and temporally variable genes (TVGs). In addition, we propose a unified framework, STAVAG (spatial- or temporal-aided framework for identifying directionally and temporally variable genes), that models spatial or temporal information to identify DVGs and TVGs. STAVAG effectively identifies biologically meaningful DVGs for uncovering prognostically relevant gene modules that align with the malignant-immune-stroma structure in the tumor microenvironment, identifying marker genes in three-dimensional brain data and detecting 12 polarization genes regulating planarian regeneration. Furthermore, by tracking the progression of myocardial infarction and tissue development, STAVAG reveals critical TVGs that can serve as candidate biomarkers for the ultra-acute phase of myocardial infarction. STAVAG also identifies both global and local gene modules involved in mouse placentation, as well as tissue-specific and interactive TVG modules that dynamically evolve during mouse embryonic development.

papers.abstract: Electrolyte deficiencies and their treatment are ubiquitous in patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). We sought to conduct a narrative review of hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia, hypophosphatemia, and hypokalemia in critical care. We searched Ovid MEDLINE®, Embase®, Cochrane CENTRAL, and reference lists for information relevant to the physiology, epidemiology, and treatment of electrolyte deficiencies in adults with critical illness. We also looked for information about financial costs and environmental impact of treatment. Electrolyte deficiencies are common in patients admitted to the ICU, with prevalences of 55-88% for hypocalcemia, 27-66% for hypomagnesemia, 15-53% for hypophosphatemia, and 17-50% for hypokalemia. Neuromuscular and cardiovascular symptoms are common to all four deficiencies, and the benefits and harms of routine or protocolized treatment are uncertain. Calcium replacement is potentially fraught, with possible harm in cardiac arrest data, lack of any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating replacement, and difficulties diagnosing deficiency outside of ionized calcium measurement. Prophylactic magnesium administration may prevent postoperative atrial fibrillation in patients undergoing cardiac surgery, but whether protocolized replacement reduces atrial fibrillation or mortality in patients with critical illness without cardiac problems is uncertain. Phosphate replacement may be relevant to ventilator weaning and ICU-acquired weakness, owing to its physiologic role in cellular energy and available clinical data. Potassium replacement has been investigated in large observational studies and an RCT, indicating that higher thresholds are not superior to lower ones. Enteral replacement is associated with lower costs and less environmental impact compared with the intravenous route. Electrolyte deficiencies and their treatment are common in adult patients admitted to the ICU. The impact of particular thresholds and dosing strategies for treatment on patient outcomes, resource use, and the environment remain important areas for future research.

papers.abstract: Ipilimumab plus nivolumab is standard first-line treatment for patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (mccRCC). The aim of the A031704/PDIGREE trial was to evaluate an ipilimumab-nivolumab-based, response-adapted treatment strategy to establish its optimal implementation. In this adaptive, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial, we enrolled patients aged 18 years or older with International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium (IMDC) intermediate-risk or poor-risk mccRCC at 258 study sites (academic, regional, and community centres) in the USA. During step 1 of the study, participants were treated with up to four cycles of 1 mg/kg intravenous ipilimumab and 3 mg/kg intravenous nivolumab once every 3 weeks. At 12 weeks, step 2 treatment with nivolumab with or without cabozantinib was assigned by Immunotherapy Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours response. Patients randomly assigned to nivolumab alone received nivolumab 480 mg intravenously once every 4 weeks, and those assigned to nivolumab plus cabozantinib received nivolumab 80 mg intravenously once every 4 weeks plus cabozantinib 40 mg orally once per day. The study was open label. The primary outcome is event-driven 3-year overall survival. This Article is a prespecified report of patient demographics, treatment withdrawals during step 1, and adverse events that occurred during step 1 in all patients who received at least one dose of ipilimumab-nivolumab. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03793166) and is ongoing. From June 7, 2019, to May 15, 2024, 1111 patients were enrolled to step 1, of whom 1093 received at least one dose of ipilimumab-nivolumab and were evaluable for adverse events. In step 1, median age was 64·0 years (range 29·0-86·0), 819 (73·7%) were male, and 292 (26·3%) were female; 945 (85·1%) patients were White, 47 (4·2%) were Black, 36 (3·2%) were Asian, 14 (1·3%) were American Indian or Alaska Native, and 115 (10·4%) self-reported to have Hispanic ethnicity. 365 patients discontinued treatment during step 1 and 746 patients were enrolled to step 2. In step 2, 141 patients with progressive disease were treated with cabozantinib, nine patients with complete response were treated with nivolumab, and 596 patients with partial response or stable disease were randomly assigned to nivolumab (n=298) or nivolumab-cabozantinib (n=298). Fewer patients in step 2 had poor-risk disease (21·0% vs 27·6%; p=0·014) or bone metastases (24·4% vs 34·1%; p=0·0007) compared with the overall population who enrolled in step 1. The most common grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events during step 1 were diarrhoea (53 [4·8%] of 1093 participants) and elevated alanine aminotransferase (39 [3·6%]). There were 44 deaths, 15 (34·1%) of which were attributed as possibly related to treatment. To our knowledge, PDIGREE has enrolled and treated the largest mccRCC population with ipilimumab-nivolumab to date. Despite the real-world setting and relatively poor-risk population, there were no new safety signals compared with those reported in previous of ipilimumab-nivolumab and cabozantinib-nivolumab in first-line mccRCC. These findings support use of first-line ipilimumab-nivolumab before a response-adapted treatment strategy. National Institutes of Health.

papers.abstract: Despite successful surgical resection, many patients with skull base meningiomas experience persistent neurological and neuropsychological deficits. Diffusion tensor imaging enables characterization of white matter microstructural integrity, yet longitudinal studies remain scarce. This study examined longitudinal white matter tract changes in patients with olfactory groove meningiomas. This prospective study included 35 patients with olfactory groove meningiomas who underwent comprehensive preoperative and long-term postoperative (n = 25, ≥ 6 months) clinical, neuropsychological, and neuroimaging assessments, along with 20 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Diffusion tensor imaging was acquired on a 3T scanner, and 11 white matter tracts were reconstructed in each participant. Linear mixed models compared diffusion metrics across groups. Multivariable regression, cluster analysis, and ROC analysis identified predictors of white matter recovery. Preoperatively, patients showed widespread microstructural alterations in the uncinate fasciculus, inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus, anterior thalamic radiation, and forceps minor. Only the left uncinate fasciculus showed significant postoperative increase in axial diffusivity (p = 0.003), though values remained below those of healthy controls. Peritumoral edema volume was the strongest predictor of these alterations, explaining approximately 50% of variance (R² = 0.49-0.60, p 41,145 mm³ discriminated the cluster with little or no postoperative diffusion change (AUC = 0.93). Cluster analysis of postoperative changes in axial diffusivity identified two patterns: little or no change in 24% of patients (n = 6) and moderate change in 76% (n = 19). No significant correlations were found between tract-specific changes and clinical outcomes. Postoperative alterations in white matter diffusion metrics is limited and primarily determined by preoperative edema burden. Peritumoral edema may cause irreversible microstructural damage despite successful surgery, highlighting the importance of edema management. The dissociation between structural and functional outcomes underscores the need for multimodal approaches to understand postoperative recovery.

papers.abstract: High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are lethal brain tumors affecting both pediatric and adult patients and lack effective treatments. Previous work suggested a role for menin inhibition in suppression H3K27M diffuse midline glioma. Here we explore the potential of menin as a therapeutic target in high grade glioma and develop new compounds with improved pharmacokinetics and enhanced anti-glioma activity. A new set of molecules based on the scaffold of the first generation menin inhibitor MI-2-2 were designed and synthesized by exchanging metabolically active moieties. Activity and specificity were evaluated in genetically engineered MEN1-WT and KO glioma cells. Further anti-glioma effects were assessed in a panel of patient-derived H3K27M DMG lines and adult histone wild type HGG lines in vitro and in vivo using intracranial xenograft mouse models. We developed a new compound, MY-182, which effectively inhibits both H3K27M DMGs (IC50 range: 14.9 nM to 350.4 nM) and adult HGGs (IC50range: 0.25 μm to 4 μm) viability. We demonstrate that menin deletion significantly decreases glioma growth in vitro and in vivo. Both silencing MEN1 and treatment of MY-182 result in DNA-damage related cell death and suppression of oncogenes and markers of glioma stem/progenitor-like cells. Furthermore, MY-182 treatment was able to inhibit tumor growth in vivo. Our findings suggest a relevant role for menin in glioma initiation and maintenance in both pediatric and adult high-grade glioma. We have developed a new compound that shows enhanced anti-glioma activity.

papers.abstract: Management of peritoneal carcinomatosis (PC) is limited by subjective visual staging using the Peritoneal Cancer Index (PCI) and low sensitivity of cytology and blood biomarkers. Here, we evaluated the feasibility, detection rate, and prognostic value of peritoneal fluid tumor DNA (ptDNA) as a quantitative biomarker of PC burden. Sixty-three peritoneal fluid samples were collected intraoperatively from 39 patients with PC from GI cancers and analyzed using low-pass whole-genome sequencing and copy number analysis to determine tumor-derived DNA fraction (TF). Primary outcomes were ptDNA detection rate and the association between baseline ptDNA TF and overall survival (OS), evaluated using Cox models with TF and PCI as continuous variables. Secondary outcomes included comparison with cytology, PCI, and longitudinal tracking of TF during therapy. The median age of patients was 63.9 years (range, 31.2-76.0), and 19 patients (48.7%) were female. ptDNA was detected in ≥1 sample from 30 patients (76.9%), including 27 baseline samples (71.1%), and 12 of 26 samples with negative cytology (46.2%). Higher baseline TF was associated with worse OS (hazard ratio [HR] per 10% increase, 1.96 [95% CI, 1.41 to 2.73]; P < .001) and remained informative after adjustment for PCI (HR, 2.05 per 10% [95% CI, 1.39 to 3.01]; P < .001). In 16 patients with longitudinal samples, corresponding changes in ptDNA TF and PCI were correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.65, P < .001, n = 24 sample pairs). ptDNA is a quantitative and objective biomarker, frequently detected in patients with PC, that provides prognostic information independent of visual PCI assessment. ptDNA analysis could improve risk stratification and response monitoring during intraperitoneal chemotherapy.

papers.abstract: Helicobacter pylori infects half of the global population and is a major driver of gastric cancer. Clinical eradication remains challenging because antibiotics must survive the acidic gastric lumen, penetrate the viscoelastic mucus barrier, and reach bacteria residing near the gastric epithelium. Here, we report a biomimetic oral delivery system that integrates rod-shaped morphology, acid protection, active mucolysis, and localized antibiotic delivery. The platform consists of clarithromycin-loaded Santa Barbara Amorphous-15 silica microrods coated with a pH-responsive alginate-pronase conjugate. The coating protects clarithromycin and pronase under acidic gastric conditions, while the less acidic inner mucus microenvironment promotes coating detachment and pronase-mediated mucolysis, enabling active mucus penetration. In vitro and in vivo studies show that these bacteria-mimicking microrods significantly enhance mucus penetration and increase gastric residence time twofold. In a murine infection model, the platform achieved 100% eradication at 15 milligrams per kilogram and maintained 90% clearance at 7.5 milligrams per kilogram, producing a ∼2000-fold bacterial burden reduction compared to free clarithromycin. This bioinspired, shape-guided strategy offers a promising paradigm for localized gastrointestinal therapy.

papers.abstract: A multiplicity of translesion synthesis (TLS) DNA polymerases (Pols) promote replication through DNA lesions in an error-free or error-prone manner. Among these Pols, Polθ operates in an error-prone manner. However, Polθ conducts TLS in human cells in a much more error-free manner than implicated from the high error-proneness of the purified Pol. To resolve this incongruity, here we show that the TREX1/TREX2 3' → 5' exonucleases are integral components of TLS mediated by Polθ. In TREX1- or TREX2-deficient cells, Polθ-dependent TLS becomes nonoperational and chromosomal instability rises similar to that in Polθ-deficient cells. Consequently, similar to that in Polθ-/- mice, trex2-/- mice exhibit increased susceptibility to ultraviolet-induced skin cancers. Furthermore, our findings that in the absence of TREX1/TREX2 3' → 5' exonuclease activities, Polθ-mediated TLS manifests high mutagenicity, and an increase in the diversity of misincorporated nucleotides demarcate a crucial role of these exonucleases in the removal of Polθ misinsertions and, thereby, in enhancing Polθ TLS fidelity and the consequent genome stability.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) poses a persistent barrier to effective immunotherapy, in part due to the emergence of exhausted CD8⁺ T cells. Using a hydrodynamic, autochthonous HCC model based on Sleeping Beauty-mediated delivery of oncogenic drivers and defined OVA derived antigens, we could manipulate antigen affinity under physiological priming conditions. With this system, we examined how TCR signal strength and the transcription factor Eomesodermin (Eomes) shape CD8⁺ T cell fate in vivo. High affinity stimulation supported robust effector differentiation and the formation of tissue resident memory T cells (Trm), resulting in early tumor control. In contrast, low affinity stimulation induced elevated Eomes expression and favored rapid transition toward an exhausted (Tex) phenotype. Genetic repression of Eomes enhanced Trm differentiation in high affinity CD8⁺ T cells and delayed tumor relapse, whereas ectopic Eomes expression accelerated exhaustion and led to earlier tumor recurrence. Under low affinity conditions, Eomes deficiency increased the Trm to Tex ratio but remained insufficient to restore effective antitumor immunity, indicating that weak TCR engagement imposes constraints that cannot be overcome by Eomes loss alone. These findings reveal that the strength of TCR engagement shapes CD8⁺ T cell fate in HCC, while Eomes selectively biases this process toward exhaustion at the expense of effector and resident memory programs, ultimately influencing the durability of tumor control.

papers.abstract: Metaplastic breast cancer (MpBC) is rare, often triple-negative, and has historically had lower systemic therapy response rates and inferior outcomes compared with other breast cancer subtypes. The addition of immunotherapy to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) has led to improved pathologic complete response (pCR) rates, event-free survival, and overall survival in patients with unselected triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Whether or to what degree benefits of NAC with immunotherapy are seen in patients with MpBC is unknown. Eligible participants with nonmetastatic MpBC treated with preoperative therapy between January 2010 and June 2024 were ascertained from pathology and treatment records at the University of Pennsylvania. Two cohorts of patients were evaluated: (1) patients who received NAC and (2) patients who received NAC with immunotherapy (NACI). Objectives were to evaluate pCR and recurrence rates. Eighty-five individuals with MpBC and prior neoadjuvant therapy were identified, including 51 and 34 patients who received NAC and NACI, respectively. Rates of pCR were 17.6% with NAC and 26.5% with NACI (21.2% overall). No clinical factors were associated with pCR, including clinical stage or histopathologic subtype of MpBC. With a median follow-up of 29.6 months after surgery, distant metastatic disease developed in 52.9% and 17.6% of patients who received NAC and NACI, respectively. No patients with pCR developed distant metastatic disease. pCR rates in individuals with MpBC remain low despite the benefits of NACI seen in studies of unselected TNBC. Individuals with MpBC who experience pCR have favorable outcomes, underscoring the need to understand biomarkers of treatment response in these patients.

papers.abstract: Postoperative surveillance following pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (PanNET) resection remains based on expert consensus despite biologic heterogeneity. Current guidelines recommend surveillance for 10 years postoperatively without individual recurrence risk determination, resulting in prolonged imaging despite only a minority developing late recurrence beyond 5 years. To investigate the incidence, biologic features, and factors associated with late recurrence following resection of PanNETs and develop risk-adapted framework for individualized long-term surveillance. This multi-institutional retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing resection of localized well-differentiated PanNETs at 5 high-volume US academic centers. Exploratory molecular analyses were performed in an independent whole genome sequencing cohort. Data from January 2000 to December 2023 were collected and analyzed from May to July 2026. Surgical resection. Long-term recurrence dynamics, clinicopathologic and molecular factors associated with late recurrence, and postoperative risk stratification for individualized surveillance. Among 1769 patients undergoing pancreatic resection (median [IQR] age, 59.0 [49.5-67.9] years; 935 [52.9%] male), recurrence occurred in 255 (14.4%) after a median follow-up of 63.7 (95% CI, 60.0-67.5) months. Importantly, 851 patients remained under observation beyond 5 years postoperatively with a median follow-up of 102.8 (95% CI, 99.4-106.2) months. Competing-risk analysis demonstrated a 22.6% (95% CI, 19.8%-25.5%) cumulative incidence of recurrence at 10 years postoperatively. Smoothed hazard estimates demonstrated a recurrence peak between 2 and 5 years, followed by a persistent annual recurrence hazard of 3.5% (95% CI, 2.6%-4.4%) per person-year beyond 5 years. Multifocal disease (odds ratio, 3.90; 95% CI, 1.37-11.10; P = .01) and tumor size greater than 3 cm (odds ratio, 2.58; 95% CI, 1.15-5.79; P = .02) were independently associated with late recurrence. The Lymph Node-Negative Recurrence in Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors score demonstrated good discriminatory performance for projecting late recurrence (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.68-0.80; P < .001). For patients who had no evidence of disease at 5 years, the cumulative residual recurrence incidence was 1.2% (95% CI, 0.0%-3.0%), 11.2% (95% CI, 5.6%-16.9%), and 22.9% (95% CI, 15.3%-30.4%) for low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (P < .001). Patients with low risk demonstrated an annual recurrence hazard below 0.5% per person-year beyond 5 years. This cohort study shows that recurrence following PanNET resection can persist beyond 5 years but varies according to individual postoperative risk profile. These findings support the transition to a risk-adapted surveillance strategy, including early surveillance discontinuation after 5 years for patients at low risk and otherwise prolonged surveillance.

papers.abstract: High-dimensional proteomic profiling can improve clinical risk prediction and provide insight into disease biology, but routine acquisition of omic data at population scale remains impractical. We developed Real-world AI-based Biomarker Inference Technology (RABIT), a machine learning framework that biologically augments electronic health records (EHRs) by projecting longitudinal clinical histories into a high-dimensional proteomic representation space learned from paired EHR and plasma proteomics. RABIT was trained using patients with paired EHRs and measured plasma proteomics and externally validated in an independent cohort with paired data. RABIT profiles showed broad concordance with measured protein expression and more closely resembled measured proteomics than their input EHR. Incorporating these biologically augmented representations improved 5-year disease onset prediction across 14 conditions (n = 449,223; mean adjusted AUPRC increase of 33.7%) and generalized to an external cohort (n = 1,038,419; mean adjusted AUPRC increase of 70.3%). RABIT profiles reproduced clinically meaningful organ-specific biological changes in response to aging and further outperformed models built from comprehensive established clinical predictors in prediction of chronic kidney disease progression, major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and response to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Last, RABIT enabled biological signatures derived from small discovery cohorts to be extended to population-scale clinical datasets, generating clinically relevant hypotheses linking cytomegalovirus-associated immune states to variation in brain tumor outcomes. Together, these results demonstrate that biological augmentation of EHRs can enable molecularly informed clinical prediction and hypothesis generation at population scale.

papers.abstract: Immunotherapy has transformed the treatment of hematologic cancers, but chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapies have shown limited efficacy against solid tumors. Macrophages can infiltrate solid tumors, yet CAR macrophage therapy may be limited by systemic toxicity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. We developed a nanobody-based CAR platform targeting glypican-3 and generated CAR macrophage-derived extracellular vesicles (CAR-MEVs) as a cell-free therapeutic strategy. CAR-MEVs displayed tumor-targeting nanobodies, preferentially accumulated in glypican-3-positive tumors, and were better tolerated than CAR macrophages in mice. Across multiple murine tumor models and humanized patient-derived xenograft models, treatment with CAR-MEVs suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival. CAR-MEVs remodeled the tumor microenvironment by reducing M2-like macrophages and increasing activated neutrophils. Mechanistically, tumor-targeted CAR-MEVs delivered tumor necrosis factor-related apoptosis-inducing ligand (TRAIL), which triggered caspase-8-dependent BAP31 cleavage, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and immunogenic cell death. The resulting danger signals promoted neutrophil recruitment and antitumor activation. Neutrophil depletion and neutrophil-specific Nos2 deletion showed that therapeutic efficacy depended predominantly on neutrophils and was partly mediated by inducible nitric oxide synthase. CAR-MEVs also enhanced the activity of CD47 blockade, leading to durable tumor control and antitumor immune memory in mice. These findings support CAR-MEVs as a tumor-targeted, cell-free immunotherapy for solid tumors.

papers.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have become a key focus in cancer research due to their high stability, diversity, and ability to regulate various biological processes. This study explores the impact of small-molecule inhibition of EWS::FLI1 oncogene by YK-4-279 in Ewing sarcoma (ES). ES is a rare and highly aggressive childhood cancer driven by fusion proteins that disrupt normal gene regulation and promote tumor growth. Current treatments rely on intensive chemotherapy with serious long-term side effects, emphasizing the need for targeted therapies. A promising new approach targets the interaction between EWS::FLI1 and the RNA helicase DHX9 through the small molecule YK-4-279, which displays strong antitumor effects and has advanced to clinical trials. Transcriptome profiling revealed widespread changes in circRNA expression after YK-4-279 treatment, with a notable up-regulation of circSRSF5. Functional and mechanistic evidence identifies a key role for circSRSF5 in tumor cell survival by stabilizing the anti-apoptotic protein eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3) and contributing to therapy resistance. These findings uncover a previously unidentified role for circRNAs, particularly circSRSF5, in ES pathogenesis and treatment response.
