papers.abstract: Anthracyclines are effective chemotherapeutic agents that cause DNA and chromatin damage. One member of the anthracyclines, aclarubicin, has gained therapeutic interest due to its ability to kill cancer cells through chromatin-based mechanisms, thus avoiding the off-target effects associated with DNA damage. However, the molecular mechanism of action leading to aclarubicin-induced chromatin damage remains elusive. Here we performed Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag) of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) and other transcriptional regulators in human cells following aclarubicin treatment. We found that aclarubicin strongly disrupts the replication-coupled histone genes, resulting in a nonproductive accumulation of Pol II transcription machinery at levels exceeding those at other genes. We attribute this sensitivity to the dense Pol II loading and rapid transcription of the histone genes, which intensify the chromatin-disrupting effects of aclarubicin. Together, our findings shed light on the mechanism of aclarubicin as an anticancer drug and point to the replication-coupled histone genes as a target for therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract: Locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma (LAPC) has a low resection rate (22%). In our prior phase II study, cancer vaccination (GVAX), pembrolizumab, SBRT and chemotherapy was associated with improved distant metastasis-free survival, but increased M2-like macrophages correlated with worse survival. In preclinical models, cysteine-cysteine chemokine receptors 2 (CCR2) and 5 (CCR5) blockade overcomes macrophage-driven resistance. We therefore initiated a phase I/II trial of nivolumab and BMS-813160 (CCR2/5 inhibitor) ± GVAX with FOLFIRINOX, SBRT, and surgery for LAPC. Primary endpoints were safety and changes in intratumoral CD137+CD8+ T cells which correlate with favorable survival. Twenty-two patients were treated; the remainder had disease progression during chemotherapy, withdrew consent, or did not meet eligibility prior to study treatment. In phase I (n=9), patients received nivolumab 480mg IV, GVAX 5x108 cells intradermal q4 weeks, and BMS-813160 150mg PO BID (DL1, n=3) or 300mg PO BID (DL2, n=6) with no dose limiting toxicities. In phase II (n=13), patients were randomized to nivolumab and BMS-813160 without (Arm A) or with (Arm B) GVAX; 3/5 patients (Arm A) and 8/11 patients (Arm B + DL2) achieved the primary immunologic endpoint. Fourteen patients had paired tumor biopsies with 13 showing >80% increase in CD137+CD8+ T cells meeting the primary immunology endpoint. Fourteen (64%) of 22 treated patients underwent R0/R1 resection which was numerically higher than historical LAPC data. In conclusion, adding nivolumab, BMS-813160, and GVAX to chemo-radiotherapy is tolerable and associated with favorable immunologic and clinical outcomes, though substantial attrition before study therapy limits definitive conclusions.

papers.abstract: Urothelial carcinoma (UC) is a histologically and molecularly heterogeneous disease. Alongside pure (conventional) UC histology, approximately 25% to 40% of tumors display distinct morphologies or characteristics and are categorized as UC subtype histologies or divergent differentiation. Additionally, a small proportion of bladder cancers have pure nonurothelial histologies. Specific UC histologies are enriched within molecular subtypes, and increasing evidence has indicated that expression of therapeutic targets (eg, nectin-4, ERBB2 [formerly HER2], or FGFR3) varies by histology or molecular subtype. In this narrative review, histologic and molecular classifications of UC are introduced, including studies of therapeutic target expression, and clinical studies that have examined outcomes with first-line options for advanced UC according to tumor histology are reviewed. Patients with UC histologic subtypes or divergent differentiation are underrepresented in prospective clinical trials. Retrospective studies of first-line enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab treatment for advanced UC have suggested that outcomes may be worse in tumors with squamous differentiation (approximately 10%-15% of the overall UC population) compared with pure UC; further studies on the potential association with low nectin-4 expression are needed. Older studies have suggested that responses to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy are similar or slightly reduced compared with pure UC; however, contemporary studies are needed. In populations with disease control following platinum-based chemotherapy, outcomes with avelumab first-line maintenance treatment have been generally consistent across UC histologies, although variation between studies was observed. No treatment-by-histology interaction or direct comparison demonstrating differential benefits between first-line regimens has been reported. Additionally, most studies were retrospective, and several studies have only been reported at congresses. This review suggests that UC tumor histology may inform biological understanding and study stratification, but it is not a validated biomarker for treatment selection in advanced UC. As treatment options in UC expand, clinical advances may increasingly rely on molecular characterization.

papers.abstract: Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) for locally advanced rectal cancer is associated with substantial toxic effect burden. Sodium copper chlorophyllin has potential cytoprotective and radioprotective effects, providing a rationale for clinical validation. To determine whether prophylactic chlorophyllin improves combined acute grade 2 or higher gastrointestinal tract, hematologic, or genitourinary toxic effects during intensified TNT. This double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 randomized clinical trial accrued patients from July 2023 to October 2024 at 2 tertiary cancer centers in India. Eligible patients were 18 years or older; had nonmetastatic, locally advanced, histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the mid or low rectum; and were suitable for chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Data were analyzed from July 2023 to August 2025. Chlorophyllin, 750 mg per day, or placebo started 10 to 14 days before TNT and continued until 3 months after TNT. TNT included short-course radiotherapy, 18 weeks of chemotherapy, and brachytherapy boost. The primary outcome was incidence of acute grade 2 or higher gastrointestinal tract, hematologic, or genitourinary toxic effects by Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0. Secondary outcomes included grade 3 or higher toxic effects, treatment compliance, and all other grades of acute adverse events. Of 73 included patients, 46 (63%) were male, and the median (IQR) age was 53 (45-62) years. A total of 36 were included in the placebo group and 37 in the chlorophyllin group. A total of 52 patients (71%) had T3 disease and 58 (79%) had node-positive disease. All 73 patients completed radiation, and 14 (19%), including 10 (28%) in the placebo group and 4 (11%) in the chlorophyllin group (P = .07), needed chemotherapy dose reductions. Grade 2 or higher toxic effects occurred in 34 (94%) in the placebo group and 24 (65%) in the chlorophyllin group (absolute reduction, 29.6 percentage points; 90% CI, 15.2-43.9; risk ratio, 0.69; 90% CI, 0.56-0.86; P = .003); grade 3 or higher toxic effects occurred in 19 (53%) and 10 (27%), respectively (absolute reduction, 25.8 percentage points; 90% CI, 7.5-44.0; risk ratio, 0.51; 90% CI, 0.30-0.86; P = .03). The impact was observed with no evidence of heterogeneity detected for sex, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status score, histology, T stage, and N stage and after adjustment for chemotherapy and brachytherapy use. Compared to patients in the placebo group, patients in the chlorophyllin arm had significant improvement in grade 3 gastrointestinal tract toxic effects (8 [22%] vs 1 [3%]; P = .01), especially for grade 2 or higher proctitis, anal pain, rectal bleeding, and both grade 2 or higher and grade 3 or higher diarrhea. No unexpected serious drug-related adverse events were noted. In this phase 2 randomized clinical trial, chlorophyllin significantly improved acute treatment-related adverse events compared with placebo with no safety concerns, thereby supporting its further evaluation in a multicentric phase 3 randomized clinical trial. papers.abstract: Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is characterized by rapid progression and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and limited therapeutic responses. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to assess causal associations while minimizing confounding and reverse causation. Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 males, we identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression promoted tumor growth in mice, accompanied by activation of cholesterol metabolism, androgen receptor (AR) signaling, and immunosuppression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed CREB3L4 enrichment in human PCa cells. Interaction analysis identified enhanced growth and differentiation factor (GDF) signaling in CREB3L4+ tumor cells, with CD8+ T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand-receptor analysis and coculture experiments identified GDF15 as the key mediator, through which tumor cells suppressed CD8+ T cell proliferation and activation via TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, GDF15 neutralization attenuated CREB3L4-driven tumor growth and CD8+ T cell dysfunction, whereas prostate-specific CREB3L4 knockout or adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown suppressed tumor growth and restored CD8+ T cell function. Clinical analyses confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, inversely associated with CD8+ T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response. Collectively, these findings reveal that CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15 expression, driving CD8+ T cell dysfunction and identifying the CREB3L4-GDF15 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PCa.

papers.abstract: The United States faces evolving anesthesia workforce challenges associated with population aging, rising surgical demand, and training pipeline constraints. Understanding projected supply and demand for anesthesiology physicians and certified registered nurse anesthetists (CRNAs) is essential for workforce planning, training policy, and team-based care models. This study presents a secondary analysis of US Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) workforce projections from 2022 to 2037, accessed in December 2025. Full-time-equivalent (FTE) supply and demand were extracted for anesthesiology physicians and CRNAs at three levels of aggregation: national totals, all 50 states and the District of Columbia, and urban-rural strata. The primary outcome was adequacy, defined as the ratio of FTE supply to FTE demand. Secondary outcomes were the absolute workforce gap (supply minus demand), state-level distributional inequality (unweighted Gini coefficient and coefficient of variation [CV]), urban-rural adequacy, and 2037 adequacy under four HRSA-specified alternative supply scenarios (fewer graduates, more graduates, earlier retirement, later retirement). Because the HRSA model is deterministic, all values are point estimates without confidence intervals, and no statistical hypothesis testing was performed. National anesthesiology physician adequacy declined from 1.00 in 2022 (55,330 vs 55,330 FTEs; a value fixed by model calibration rather than observed) to 0.86 in 2037 (52,310 vs 60,760 FTEs; shortfall: 8,450 FTEs). CRNA adequacy rose from 1.00 in 2022 (59,460 vs 59,460 FTEs) to 1.14 (74,680 vs 65,300 FTEs; supply exceeding modeled demand by 9,380 FTEs). State-level physician adequacy deteriorated (median: 0.94-0.79; Gini: 0.16-0.19), while CRNA adequacy improved (median: 0.79-0.98; Gini: 0.39-0.31). Nonmetropolitan physician adequacy reached 0.24 by 2037 compared with 0.96 in metropolitan areas, versus nonmetropolitan CRNA adequacy of 1.71. Physician shortfalls persisted under all modeled scenarios (range: 0.81-0.91); CRNA supply remained above modeled demand in every scenario (range: 1.09-1.20). From 2022 to 2037, anesthesiology physician and CRNA workforces are projected to follow divergent adequacy trajectories, with geographic maldistribution and severe rural physician deficits. These deterministic projections are hypothesis-generating and support further evaluation of targeted workforce strategies that account for geographic variation, the complementary roles of each profession, and the organizational models through which anesthesia care is delivered.

papers.abstract: The treatment landscape of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) has been transformed by targeted therapies, with Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKi) becoming a cornerstone of disease management. Pirtobrutinib, the first approved non-covalent BTKi, was specifically developed to overcome resistance to covalent BTKi, while improving kinase selectivity and treatment tolerability. Initially approved for heavily pretreated patients, including those previously exposed to both BTK and BCL2 inhibitors, its clinical development has progressively expanded into earlier treatment settings. More recently, pirtobrutinib has also been approved by the Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency for treatment-naïve patients, while ongoing studies are evaluating fixed-duration combination strategies, further broadening its potential clinical applications. Despite these advances, important questions remain regarding its optimal positioning within treatment sequencing and the potential emergence of cross-resistance mutations. In this critical review, we discuss the clinical development of pirtobrutinib, its efficacy and safety profile, and its evolving role in the current CLL treatment landscape. We also examine the implications of introducing non-covalent BTK inhibition at different stages of the disease and its potential impact on subsequent therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract: Cancer remains a major public health burden worldwide, underscoring the need to identify modifiable environmental risk factors. Evidence regarding the association between long-term PM2.5 exposure and overall incident cancer remains limited. We investigated this association using the nationally representative China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). We included 14,580 participants from CHARLS who were cancer-free at baseline in 2011-2012 and followed through 2020. Long-term PM2.5 exposure was estimated using annual city-level concentrations and analyzed both continuously and by quartiles. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was used to examine potential nonlinearity, and subgroup and Fine-Gray competing risk analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the findings. During follow-up, 478 participants developed incident cancer. In the fully adjusted model, each 10 μg/m3 increase in long-term PM2.5 exposure was associated with a 13.3% higher hazard of incident cancer (HR = 1.133, 95% CI: 1.069-1.200; p < 0.001). Compared with the lowest exposure quartile, the HRs were 0.990 (95% CI: 0.747-1.311), 1.508 (95% CI: 1.166-1.951), and 1.335 (95% CI: 1.026-1.737) for Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively. RCS indicated a significant overall association (p < 0.001) with evidence of nonlinearity (p for nonlinearity = 0.041). The association remained significant in the competing risk model (sHR = 1.135, 95% CI: 1.070-1.203; p < 0.001), with no significant interactions across subgroups defined by age, chronic disease, or smoking status. Long-term PM2.5 exposure was associated with an increased risk of incident cancer among Chinese adults, with each 10 μg/m3 increase corresponding to a 13.3% higher hazard. These findings provide epidemiological evidence of an association between long-term ambient PM2.5 exposure and incident cancer among Chinese adults, highlighting the potential importance of air pollution control in cancer prevention.

papers.abstract: The therapeutic landscape for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) has evolved over recent years with new classes of agents approved and medications initially approved for mCRPC demonstrating benefit in earlier disease states. However, real-world data on contemporary treatment patterns are limited in Europe and Asia. This real-world observational cross-sectional study included men with mCRPC receiving first-line therapy in EU4 (Germany, France, Italy, Spain), the UK, Japan, and China between 2020 and 2024. Patient-level data on physician-reported mCRPC therapies were derived from the IQVIA Oncology Dynamics database. Treatment patterns were assessed according to current therapy in patients receiving first-line (1 L) to fourth and subsequent lines (4 L+) of therapy, as well as one prior line of therapy. Annual trends were described. Among 18,498 men with mCRPC included in the study, 8448 received 1 L therapy, 6861 received 2 L therapy, 2237 received 3 L therapy, and 952 received 4 L+ therapy. Androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) were the most common 1 L treatment (≥ 55%) everywhere except Germany, and the most common 2 L treatment (≥ 60%) in all countries. Notably, German patients had a higher proportion of visceral metastases. Chemotherapy was the most common 3 L and 4 L+ treatment across EU4, UK, and Asia. Radiopharmaceuticals were mainly used in later lines of treatment (LOTs), with the highest use in the UK (3 L: 10%, 4 L+: 32%). Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor use was limited in 1 L and 2 L treatment and remained generally low (≤ 10%) in 3 L and 4 L+, except for Italy (3 L: 27%, 4 L+: 17%). Men receiving ARPI for non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC) or metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) prior to 1 L mCRPC treatment often received back-to-back ARPI (12%-46% in EU4 and the UK, 21% in China and 66% in Japan). Back-to-back ARPI use between mCRPC LOTs decreased in later LOTs but was still relatively common. In real-world clinical practice, ARPIs are the mainstay of treatment across regions and LOTs, with back-to-back ARPI commonly used in most countries, both from nmCRPC/mHSPC to 1 L mCRPC and between LOTs for mCRPC. These findings highlight the need for optimised sequencing and uptake of non-ARPI options when clinically appropriate for men with mCRPC.

papers.abstract: Obesity is a risk factor for colorectal cancer (CRC), with visceral adipose tissue (VAT) playing a role as tumor microenvironment through the secretion of adipokines and promotion of insulin resistance. In this study, we evaluated transcriptomic differences in VAT of CRC patients with high versus low amounts of VAT, measured as visceral fat area (VFA). Tumor-adjacent VAT was collected in 88 Stage I-III CRC patients undergoing primary surgery as part of the ColoCare Study at Huntsman Cancer Institute (HCI), University of Utah, and Heidelberg University Hospital, Germany. Bulk transcriptomic analysis (RNAseq) was performed on VAT at the HCI genomics core. VFA was measured via computed tomography (CT) scans and categorized as low (< 196 cm2) or high (≥ 196 cm2). Differential gene expression by VFA was assessed using DESeq2, adjusting for age, study site, sex, tumor stage, and tumor site. Ranked genes were analyzed with GSEA software to identify enriched gene sets and pathways. 56% of patients were male, mean age was 64 ± 12 years, and 42% had Stage III CRC. Between patients with high VFA and low VFA, n = 284 genes were differentially expressed. GSEA identified 15 upregulated and 21 downregulated gene sets (p-adj. < 0.05). Upregulated gene sets included pathways related to homologous recombination, focal adhesion, and extracellular matrix signaling. Downregulated gene sets included pathways related to insulin signaling, oxidative phosphorylation, and adipocytokine signaling. High VFA was linked to overexpression of pathways associated with CRC development and progression. This study underscores VAT's likely role in CRC progression.

papers.abstract: Intraoperative ultrasound (iUS) provides real-time imaging during brain tumor resection, but its utility may be limited by surgical cavity collapse and distortion of surrounding anatomy. We developed a spherical ultrasound applicator intended to provide a reproducible imaging interface within the resection cavity, with the potential to support cavity geometry during post-resection assessment. This study evaluated the feasibility of applicator placement and ultrasound image acquisition across simulated resection cavity geometries and imaging conditions. A spherical applicator with a 17.5-mm radius and central ultrasound probe channel was fabricated and evaluated using silicone phantoms representing shallow, deep, and irregular resection cavities. Ultrasound imaging was performed using phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and 1% albumin as acoustic coupling media. Embedded echogenic targets at depths of approximately 3 and 5 cm were evaluated using contrast-to-noise ratios (CNR). Computed tomography was used to verify phantom geometry and applicator fit. The applicator maintained stable contact with simulated cavity surfaces and enabled visualization of cavity margins across all three phantom geometries. Echogenic targets remained detectable at depths up to 5 cm using either coupling medium. At 3 cm, CNR values were 11.88 with PBS and 11.37 with albumin, decreasing to 6.76 and 6.24, respectively, at 5 cm. Imaging depth, rather than coupling medium, was the predominant determinant of target contrast. Computed tomography confirmed phantom geometry and applicator alignment. This phantom-based feasibility study demonstrates that a spherical ultrasound applicator can provide a reproducible acoustic interface for imaging simulated brain tumor resection cavities. The device may facilitate intraoperative assessment of cavity margins and potentially complement intracavitary radiation delivery. Further in vivo evaluation is required to establish clinical utility.

papers.abstract: Reliable biomarkers for minimal residual disease (MRD) and recurrence risk following resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remain limited. We evaluated the prognostic significance of tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) during a standardized postoperative MRD window and explored longitudinal ctDNA trajectories during surveillance. Patients with nonmetastatic PDAC were prospectively enrolled. Tumor-informed ctDNA assays were generated from diagnostic biopsy or resection specimens. The primary analysis evaluated ctDNA obtained 4-6 weeks after surgery and before initiation of adjuvant therapy. Patients were classified as MRD-positive or MRD-negative at this landmark and evaluated for recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS). Longitudinal ctDNA trajectories were evaluated as an exploratory analysis. ctDNA measurements obtained after documented clinical recurrence were not used to define prognostic groups. A total of 61 patients were enrolled, tumor-informed assays were successfully generated in 50 (82.0%), and 43 patients underwent curative-intent resection and comprised the resected analytic cohort. In total, 43 patients had evaluable ctDNA within the predefined postoperative MRD window. MRD-positive patients experienced shorter RFS and OS than MRD-negative patients, with recurrence rates of 22.2% in patients who remained ctDNA-negative to 80.0% in patients with persistent ctDNA positivity, accompanied by a corresponding decline in median RFS from 26.3 to 8.7 months and median OS from not reached to 9.7 months (both global log-rank p < 0.001). Exploratory longitudinal analysis demonstrated progressively worse outcomes among patients developing or maintaining detectable ctDNA during surveillance, with persistent ctDNA positivity identifying the highest-risk subgroup. Detection of tumor-informed ctDNA during a standardized postoperative MRD window was associated with adverse oncologic outcomes following curative-intent resection of PDAC. Longitudinal ctDNA trajectories provided additional hypothesis-generating information regarding molecular clearance and recurrence. These findings support prospective validation of postoperative ctDNA as a risk-stratification biomarker in resected PDAC.

papers.abstract: Benchmarking surgical outcomes using local data is a key component of healthcare quality improvement. International groups have outlined a range of benchmarks for pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) but there are currently no benchmarks using Australian data. This study aimed to use existing Australian registry data to develop benchmarks for PD. Retrospective cohort study based on existing data from two pancreatic cancer registries in Australia-the Upper Gastrointestinal Cancer Registry and the Pancreatic Cancer: Understanding Routine Practice and Lifting End Results Registry. Established methodologies were used to develop benchmarks for surgical outcomes for patients undergoing PD for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) for each registry, de-identified to Registry A and B. Registry A included 602 PDAC patients from 18 hospitals, and Registry B included 496 patients from 15 hospitals. The surgical outcomes available to benchmark for Registry A were lymph node yield and microscopically positive surgical margin (R1) status. Registry B had these outcomes in addition to inpatient mortality, readmission rate (within 30 days), and survival. Results were similar to international comparisons. This study presents the first published benchmarks for PD in Australia, representing the best currently available data and showcasing the substantial work of existing Australian registries, while also highlighting that there are substantial opportunities for dataset expansion. Locally developed benchmarks for the outcomes specified as core indicators by international bodies should be the minimum goal, with collection of other key outcomes providing richer data.

papers.abstract: We evaluated associations of EHRsupport, an electronic health record (EHR)-based social support measure, with breast cancer (BC) treatment and clinical outcomes in the Kaiser Permanente Northern California (KPNC) population. This study included 45,717 women from KPNC, an integrated health care system, who were diagnosed with invasive BC from January 2006-June 2024 and had social support terms in the EHR. The EHRsupport score included information about a spouse/partner, children, (clinical) visit support, living situation (alone or with others), friend/other support, positive social support, negative (lack of) social support, death of a social tie, transportation issues, relationship conflict/stress, social isolation, and emergency contact within state. We used log-binomial regression, logistic regression, and modified Poisson regression, and survival analysis to evaluate associations. The lowest (vs. highest) tertile of EHRsupport was associated with nonreceipt of surgery (odds ratio (OR)=1.46, 95% confidence interval (CI):1.27-1.67), nonreceipt of chemotherapy (risk ratio (RR)=1.20, 95% CI:1.12-1.29), surgery delays (risk ratio (RR)=1.15, 95% CI:1.11-1.20), chemotherapy delays (RR = 1.20, 95% CI:1.10-1.31), adjuvant endocrine therapy (AET) noninitiation (RR = 1.14, 95% CI:1.10-1.18), AET discontinuation (hazard ratio (HR)=1.31, 95% CI:1.24-1.39), cancer-specific mortality (HR = 1.18, 95% CI:1.08-1.28), and overall mortality (HR = 1.21, 95% CI:1.14-1.29) (p-continuous for outcomes <0.001). Associations with most treatment outcomes did not differ by race though they appeared stronger in patients with later (II and III/IV) vs. earlier stage (0/I) cancer. Associations with overall mortality were stronger in non-Hispanic White and Asian (vs. Black and Hispanic) women. EHRsupport was related to BC treatment and clinical outcomes, supporting its use as a clinical tool and research measure.

papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is associated with multiple cancers, but evidence on its prevalence and genotype distribution across anogenital sites remains limited. We analyzed baseline data from a Phase III clinical trial of a nine-valent HPV vaccine conducted in China, between September and December 2020. About 9327 healthy women aged 18-45 years were enrolled. Cervical, vulvar, and perianal swabs were collected for HPV genotyping. Cervical cytology was evaluated by pathologists. Women with abnormal cytology underwent colposcopy and, if indicated, biopsy for histopathological diagnosis. In our study, approximately 12.6% (1174/9327) of participants had abnormal cervical cytology, and 2.1% (194/9324) were diagnosed with CIN1+. Among the three anatomical sites, HPV prevalence was highest in the vulva (22.43%), followed by the perianal area (17.65%) and the cervix (14.15%). Multiple HPV infections were more common at noncervical sites (vulva: 33.17%; perianal: 30.19%) than at the cervix (24.94%). Participants with cervical HPV infection were more likely to have concurrent vulvar or perianal infection; HPV16 accounted for the highest proportion of three-site infections (47.26%). Furthermore, while the consistency of high-risk HPV types across the three anatomical sites was moderate in the overall trial population, the kappa values were markedly higher in participants with abnormal cytology. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of HPV prevalence and type distribution across multiple anogenital sites in Chinese women aged 18-45 years and serves as an essential baseline for evaluating the multi-site impact of HPV vaccination and for informing future cervical cancer screening and surveillance strategies.

papers.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a prevalent microvascular complication, remains a leading cause of irreversible vision loss globally. Traditional DR managements, including anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) intravitreal injections, are limited by high treatment burden, suboptimal patient adherence, and transient efficacy. In recent years, gene therapy has represented a promising alternative, enabling long-term, adjustable, and endogenous production of therapeutic agents through a single administration. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current understanding of DR from epidemiology, multimodal diagnosis, and molecular pathogenesis to the historical evolution and limitations of conventional therapies. Building upon these mechanistic insights, we further discuss recent advances in gene therapy for DR, extending beyond conventional anti-angiogenic strategies toward neurovascular unit protection, inflammation modulation, and metabolic regulation. Emerging gene-editing technologies, including Cas13-based RNA editing and prime editing (PE) for DNA correction, are also highlighted as promising next-generation therapeutic platforms. In addition, we summarized pioneering candidates in clinical trials, such as RGX-314, ADVM-022, and 4D-150, which have demonstrated promising efficacy in reducing the frequency of injections. Despite promising advances, we also discussed remaining challenges involving vector optimization, immune safety, transgene regulation, disease modeling, and patient stratification. Overall, gene therapy holds substantial potential to transform DR management from repetitive symptomatic intervention toward durable and personalized molecular treatment.

papers.abstract: Relapse after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) remains a barrier to cure in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Although second HSCT (HSCT2) and targeted therapies have expanded salvage options, how relapse management has evolved over time remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed 240 adults with AML who relapsed after first HSCT (HSCT1), categorized by relapse year into Group 1 (G1, 1988-2017; n = 162) and Group 2 (G2, 2018-2022; n = 78). The 2-year overall survival (OS) from relapse was 9.9% in G1 and 18.2% in G2. Multivariable analysis showed that relapse in G2 was significantly associated with better OS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.60; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.85). Among patients achieving complete remission (CR) after relapse, 2-year OS from CR was significantly higher in G2 than in G1 (52.9% vs. 27.9%; p = 0.014). The 2-year OS from HSCT2 was 18.5% in G1 and 27.3% in G2 (p = 0.14), whereas progression-free survival was significantly higher in G2 than in G1 (24.1% vs. 14.8%; p = 0.049). Long-term survivors followed heterogeneous pathways, including HSCT2 despite chemoresistant disease (n = 5) and FLT3 inhibitor-based control without HSCT2 (n = 3). An exploratory next-generation sequencing analysis included 37 G2 patients with profiles available. The frequently detected mutations were TP53 (n = 9), FLT3-ITD (n = 9), DNMT3A (n = 8), and NRAS (n = 7). In the multivariable analysis, relapse ≥ 200 days after HSCT1 was associated with better OS (HR, 0.22; 95% CI, 0.08-0.63), whereas TP53 mutations were associated with worse OS (HR, 6.84; 95% CI, 2.34-20.00). In conclusion, survival after relapse improved in the contemporary era, particularly after CR. Long-term survival was achieved through diverse salvage pathways, whereas early relapse and TP53 mutation remained challenges requiring individualized treatment strategies.

papers.abstract: Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitors have transformed frontline mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) therapy, yet existing network meta-analyses predate the pivotal trials. We performed an updated network meta-analysis of contemporary frontline regimens. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov for randomized trials of frontline MCL therapy. Transplant-ineligible, transplant-eligible and maintenance settings were analyzed as separate frequentist networks; treatments were ranked by P-scores and certainty assessed with CINeMA. Eleven of 19 eligible trials (4135 patients) formed the networks. In transplant-ineligible disease, acalabrutinib plus bendamustine-rituximab (BR; hazard ratio [HR] 0.33, 95% CI 0.21-0.53) and ibrutinib plus BR (HR 0.36, 0.23-0.57) ranked highest for progression-free survival (PFS) but neither improved overall survival (OS) (HR 0.86 and 0.98). In transplant-eligible disease, ibrutinib-containing induction ranked best for failure-free survival with (HR 0.35, 0.24-0.53) or without autologous stem-cell transplantation (ASCT; HR 0.39, 0.26-0.57), and both strategies improved OS in TRIANGLE. Rituximab- or lenalidomide-based maintenance prolonged PFS, although the OS benefit of rituximab maintenance was not sustained at long-term LyMa follow-up. Certainty was moderate at best. BTK-inhibitor-bendamustine combinations rank highest for delaying progression in transplant-ineligible MCL but did not improve OS, whereas ibrutinib-containing induction improved OS in transplant-eligible patients and renders ASCT dispensable. Resting largely on indirect evidence, these rankings should inform, not dictate, treatment while mature survival data are awaited. TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero [CRD420261439288].

papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is an aggressive and common subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Although ADAM28 is expressed in various cancers, it is considered a gene with ambivalent prognosis, and its association with clinical outcomes in DLBCL requires further investigation. This study aimed to elucidate the association between ADAM28 expression and survival in DLBCL patients. We collected gene expression and clinical data from 952 DLBCL patients in the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Multiple GSE datasets demonstrated that DLBCL patients with high ADAM28 expression had significantly better prognosis than those with low expression (OS and PFS, p < 0.05). Similarly, among patients treated with R-CHOP and those achieving complete remission or partial remission after chemotherapy, high ADAM28 expression was also associated with significantly better prognosis. Furthermore, we constructed a prognostic model for DLBCL patients based on ADAM28 expression and clinical data, which demonstrated good performance. Single-cell transcriptomic profiling revealed cellular heterogeneity within the DLBCL tumor microenvironment; ADAM28 was highly expressed in B cells (including malignant B cells) and was significantly enriched in immune-related pathways such as leukocyte cell-cell adhesion and antigen presentation. Overall, high expression of ADAM28 gene is associated with better prognosis in DLBCL patients and can serve as a biomarker for evaluating the prognosis of DLBCL patients.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4) and the programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)/programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) axis have transformed the treatment of many malignancies and can produce durable, sometimes curative, responses. Nevertheless, the majority of patients either fail to respond at the outset (primary resistance), respond transiently, or relapse after an initial benefit (acquired resistance). Resistance to immunotherapy is multifactorial and arises from a dynamic interplay between tumor-intrinsic alterations and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Tumor-intrinsic mechanisms include defects in antigen presentation such as loss of beta-2-microglobulin and human leukocyte antigen, a paucity of immunogenic neoantigens, oncogenic signaling that excludes T cells (for example WNT/beta-catenin activation and PTEN loss), and disruption of interferon-gamma signaling through JAK1/2 mutations. Within the TME, regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, tumor-associated macrophages, and cancer-associated fibroblasts collaborate with metabolic constraints, hypoxia, and inhibitory cytokines such as transforming growth factor-beta to restrain effective antitumor immunity, while chronic antigen exposure drives an epigenetically fixed state of T-cell exhaustion. Co-inhibitory receptors including LAG-3, TIM-3, and TIGIT, and the composition of the gut microbiome, further modulate therapeutic outcomes. This review summarizes the principal mechanisms underlying resistance to cancer immunotherapy, with particular emphasis on the contribution of the TME, surveys predictive biomarkers, and outlines rational combination strategies designed to convert immunologically "cold" tumors into "hot", treatment-responsive lesions. A mechanistic understanding of resistance is essential for the design of next-generation, biomarker-guided immunotherapeutic approaches.

papers.abstract: Aneuploidy, resulting from whole-chromosome or segmental gains and losses, is generally detrimental to organismal fitness and is strongly associated with tumorigenesis. While sex chromosome aneuploidies are relatively well tolerated due to dedicated allelic dosage compensation mechanisms, the existence of comparable regulatory processes for autosomes remains debated. Here, we investigate transcriptional responses to autosomal aneuploidy and identify widespread dosage compensation across affected chromosomes. Using high-sensitivity allele-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing of monoclonal cell expansions spanning diverse ploidies and degrees of aneuploidy, we uncover consistent transcriptional compensation of both chromosomal gains and losses. This response operates in a region-specific manner across both complete and segmental aneuploidies, revealing an unexpected flexibility in dosage regulation. We show that chromosome losses are compensated through increased transcriptional burst frequency from the remaining allele. Complementary proteomics analyses demonstrate additional buffering at the protein level, resulting in a substantial, though still incomplete, restoration of stoichiometric balance across autosomal aneuploid chromosomes for both copy number gains and losses. Analyses of cancer transcriptomes confirm that compensatory mechanisms are active in human tumours. Together, our findings establish dosage compensation as a genome-wide and dynamic response to gene dose imbalance. This mechanism extends beyond sex chromosomes, supports transcriptional homeostasis, and represents a fundamental and evolutionarily conserved mode of gene regulation active across species and in aneuploid cancer cells.

papers.abstract: Adjuvant therapies for breast cancer have an impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Prior studies reported worse HRQoL with endocrine therapy than with radiation therapy (RT). In the POWER trial, patients received preoperative endocrine therapy (pre-ET) to assess tolerability and guide RT decisions. The study assessed whether HRQoL was preserved across adjuvant treatment combinations and whether HRQoL during pre-ET was associated with endocrine therapy adherence. The POWER trial participants received 90 days of pre-ET. Their HRQoL was measured using the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) Quality of Life Questionnaire (QLQ)-C30 and BR23 questionnaire before and after pre-ET, at adjuvant therapy initiation, and 6 and 12 months postoperatively. The patients were grouped by RT receipt and adherence to adjuvant ET (AET) at 12-months: +RT/+AET, +RT/-AET, -RT/+AET, and -RT/-AET. The primary endpoint was change in global HRQoL from pre-ET completion to 12-months. A ≥5-point change was considered clinically meaningful. The 73 patients who completed HRQoL surveys had a mean age of 73.6 ± 6 years, and 90.4 % were Non-Hispanic white. At 12 months, the treatment groups included 39 patients (53.4 %) with -RT/+AET, 20 patients (27.4 %) with +RT/+AET, 10 patients (13.7 %) with +RT/-AET, and 4 patients (5.5 %) with -RT/-AET. The median HRQoL scores remained stable at 83.3 (IQR, 66.7-91.7) from pre-ET completion to 12 months, with similar C30 and BR23 subscale changes across the groups. At the individual level, 22 patients (30.1 %) had a clinically meaningful decline, 23 patients (31.5 %) improved, and 38.4 % had no meaningful change in global HRQoL. During pre-ET, HRQoL was not associated with AET adherence. Although adjuvant therapies are known to affect HRQoL, receipt of pre-ET may mitigate their detrimental effects on HRQoL by informing treatment decisions.

papers.abstract: Familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) is an autosomal dominant syndrome caused by inactivating APC mutations, with near-complete penetrance of colorectal cancer,1 making risk-reducing total proctocolectomy the standard treatment.2 The anastomotic technique is a key determinant of postoperative outcomes, particularly anastomotic leak.3,4 We present a totally robotic total proctocolectomy with J-pouch reconstruction using a single-stapled ileal pouch-anal anastomosis. A 16-year-old male with a positive genetic panel for FAP and colonoscopy showing pancolonic and rectal polyposis not amenable to rectal preservation underwent totally robotic total proctocolectomy with J-pouch ileal reconstruction and a diverting loop ileostomy (da Vinci Xi).5,6 The distal rectum was transected at a site previously marked by a cerclage placed 2 cm from the dentate line; a polyp in the rectal cuff was removed by robotic polypectomy. The single-stapled anastomosis was performed intracorporeally with a purse-string suture (barbed unidirectional Stratafix 2-0) around the pin of a 31-mm circular stapler (CDH), coupled to the anvil seated in the ileal pouch.3 Perfusion was confirmed with indocyanine green. The procedure was completed entirely robotically, with a favorable postoperative course. Control examinations at 3 months showed no evidence of anastomotic fistula. By eliminating the transverse staple line of the rectal cuff, the single-stapled technique avoids staple-line crossing and the associated ischemia and tension.4,7 Performed robotically, it is a safe alternative for patients undergoing risk-reducing total proctocolectomy with ileal pouch reconstruction,3,4 with potential for fewer complications and improved long-term function.8 VIDEO DESCRIPTION: Accompanying streaming video (English narration, duration under 9 min) demonstrating totally robotic total proctocolectomy with J-pouch ileal reconstruction and single-stapled ileal pouch-anal anastomosis in an adolescent with familial adenomatous polyposis.

papers.abstract: For patients with renal cell carcinoma and liver metastases, technical resectability offers only a partial basis for treatment selection. Whether local control translates into lasting clinical benefit remains uncertain. This Mini Review examines hepatic resection, percutaneous ablation (radiofrequency, microwave, cryoablation, and selected irreversible electroporation), stereotactic radiotherapy, and transarterial approaches (yttrium-90 radioembolization, chemoembolization, and embolization) in relation to contemporary systemic treatment. Small hepatic cohorts report prolonged survival in selected patients, although disease tempo, extrahepatic burden, and treatment era complicate interpretation. Prospective studies of metastasis-directed radiotherapy suggest that some patients can defer systemic therapy or continue an otherwise effective regimen; liver-specific outcomes remain poorly defined. Immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations have broadened systemic options, but response alone has not been validated as a criterion for subsequent hepatectomy. Adjuvant pembrolizumab raises a separate question: the trial-defined population with completely resected metastatic disease differs from patients receiving salvage liver treatment after systemic therapy. Molecular profiling, radiogenomics, and circulating tumor DNA offer ways to characterize disease, yet their value for selecting hepatic intervention is still unproven. We consider how hepatic anatomy, observed disease behavior, physiological reserve, and patient priorities can guide multidisciplinary discussion. Comparisons beginning at a common treatment decision point, with attention to morbidity and disruption of systemic care, are needed to clarify when liver-directed treatment adds clinically meaningful benefit.

papers.abstract: In Algeria, 5-year survival for breast cancer (BC) has improved over the past three decades, but drivers of the remaining survival deficits need to be assessed. Within the population-based cancer registry of Batna, northeastern Algeria, we assessed survival (overall and net) and its determinants among women diagnosed with BC during 2010-2012. Vital status was retrospectively ascertained through hospital and civil registration data, as well as telephone calls, whilst sociodemographic and clinical data were extracted from medical records. In total, 366 women were included; mean ± SD age at diagnosis was 48 ± 12 years. Clinical-epidemiologic data were available for 302 (83%). After 5 years, 68/366 (19%) women had died, 278 (76%) were alive, and 20 (5%) were lost to follow-up, rendering 5-year overall survival of 81% (95% CI: 76, 85) and net survival of 84% (80, 88). After mutual adjustment, TNM Stage III/IV (n = 169/284, 60%) accounted for 55% of deaths, while suboptimal treatment (no surgery, 24%, or no chemotherapy, 4%, or no radiotherapy, 31%) accounted for an additional 22%. Diabetes was also associated with higher mortality, based on a small sample. These findings indicate relatively high five-year survival after BC diagnosis; nevertheless, survival gains through earlier BC detection and improving access to comprehensive BC treatment could further reduce deaths in this setting.

papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a risk factor for head and neck cancer (HNC), but the effects of antidiabetic drugs on this risk are unclear. We evaluated glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) using the TriNetX US electronic health record database, while investigating the molecular role of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) in HNC. Adults ≥ 40 years with newly diagnosed T2DM (2012-2024) were studied retrospectively. Among > 250 million records, 105,605 GLP-1RA users were propensity-score matched 1:1 with 105,605 nonusers. Over a median 5-year follow-up, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower risks of incident HNC (HR: 0.723; 95% CI: 0.617-0.848) and all-cause mortality (HR: 0.737; 95% CI: 0.715-0.759). Results remained consistent across sex, age, obesity, smoking, alcohol use, GLP-1RA type, and further sensitivity analyses. Molecular analyses showed that higher GLP1R expression was associated with better overall survival in The Cancer Genome Atlas Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (TCGA-HNSC). GLP1R expression progressively decreased from normal to tumor and metastatic tissues, correlated with oncogenic mutation status, and was inversely associated with cell-cycle programs. In an independent multi-institutional biobank (Tri-VGH Biobank), GLP1R expression was significantly lower in tumor than matched adjacent non-tumor tissues (27 pairs), findings confirmed by tumor immunofluorescence. Overall, these epidemiological and molecular findings support a potential protective role of GLP-1RA/GLP1R signaling in HNC.

papers.abstract: Paraaortic lymph node metastases (PALNM) can be found in up to 2% of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and are considered as a risk factor for poor survival. We aimed to systematically review the literature for comparison of treatment and potential survival benefit. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were explored with specific search strategies. Studies published between January 2000 and September 2026 discussing colorectal patients with isolated PALNM, synchronous or metachronous, were included. A total of 20 articles focusing on synchronous PALNM were evaluated. Paraaortic lymph node dissection (PALND) was performed in 1385 patients with radiological suspicion of synchronous PALNM. Treatment-related morbidity rates varied from 7.8% to 31.0%. The 5-year overall survival ranged from 19.5% to 76.1%, while 5-year disease-free survival varied between 17.1% and 28.1%. Recurrence rates varied between 56.3% and 77.8%. Additionally, the articles discussing both synchronous and metachronous PALNM were comprised of 457 patients undergoing PALND. In these cases, perioperative morbidity rate ranged from 15.5% to 51.6%. The 5-year overall survival after PALND varied between 21.4% and 61.1%, while recurrence rates ranged from 31.0% to 83.9%. Colorectal metastases in the PALN remain associated with poor survival outcomes. A multidisciplinary approach using PALND and adjuvant chemotherapy or chemoradiation may increase overall and disease-free survival, comparable to outcomes after resection of colorectal liver metastasis. Furthermore, no significant increase in morbidity could be observed compared with regional lymphadenectomy alone. Even though survival outcomes might benefit from PALND, recurrence rates remain high.

papers.abstract: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes (ETMR) is a rare and highly aggressive malignant pediatric brain tumor with limited treatments. The spatial organization of the ETMR immune microenvironment remains poorly understood, limiting our understanding of tumor-immune interactions and their potential therapeutic relevance. We defined the spatial organization of ETMR using spatial transcriptomics across 11 samples from 9 patients, integrated with independent publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Immune cells were largely excluded from the tumor core, while the peritumoral border formed an immunosuppressive niche enriched for B-cells and M2-like macrophages. These cells exhibited conserved transcriptional programs associated with gliosis, extracellular matrix generation, immune suppression, and cellular exhaustion. At this interface, the CD74-MIF signaling axis was enriched, suggesting a possible coordinated mechanism underlying peritumoral macrophage and regulatory B-cell abundance. Integration with the ETMR developmental continuum further revealed spatial covariation between tumor developmental states and immune and stromal features. Multilayered rosettes, a histopathological hallmark of ETMR, showed spatially confined interferon-responsive, immune-associated transcriptional programs, enriched for type I and II interferon signaling and antigen-processing pathways. This suggests that despite global immune exclusion, localized regions of interferon-responsive and immune-associated transcriptional activity persist within the tumor. These findings define a compartmentalized spatial immune architecture in ETMR characterized by relative immune depletion in tumor-rich regions, immunoregulatory and stroma-associated programs at selected tumor interfaces, and localized interferon-responsive transcriptional activity within rosette-associated regions. This spatial framework provides a basis for future mechanistic studies of tumor-immune interactions and their potential therapeutic relevance in ETMR.

papers.abstract: Implantable spinal cord stimulators (SCSs) for the treatment of refractory neuropathic pain are becoming increasingly common in patients presenting for surgery, and their presence has important implications for anesthetic care. This is particularly relevant in obstetric anesthesia, where neuraxial techniques are routinely employed for labour analgesia and anesthesia for Cesarean delivery. In this Continuing Professional Development module, we synthesize the available case experience from the literature and provide practical recommendations to guide anesthesiologists in the perioperative management of obstetric patients with an SCS. Numerous case reports describe the safe use of both epidural and spinal anesthetic techniques in obstetric patients with an SCS. All obstetric patients with an SCS should undergo antenatal consultation with an anesthesiologist and neuromodulation specialist (usually a pain medicine physician or neurosurgeon) responsible for managing the device. Preprocedural planning, including review of relevant imaging and a focused physical examination, is essential to minimize the risk of device damage. Ultrasound can be used to assist the provider in identifying a safe neuraxial access point and may also help to improve first-pass success. The literature suggests that prior implantation of SCS components within the epidural space may be associated with a higher risk of SCS lead movement, potential for infection, and inadequate epidural labour analgesia and surgical anesthesia. In contrast, the success of spinal anesthesia for Cesarean delivery appears largely unaffected by the presence of neurostimulation leads. In patients undergoing Cesarean delivery, management considerations include temporary device inactivation, minimizing the use of monopolar cautery, and being familiar with the course of the device's leads from the impulse generator to the stimulating electrode to avoid inadvertent surgical damage. Neuraxial anesthesia is feasible and generally safe for obstetric patients with an SCS but requires careful planning and awareness of unique risks. Antenatal anesthesiology and neuromodulation consultation, imaging review, ultrasound guidance, and patient counselling can help optimize outcomes and minimize complications.

papers.abstract: Patients with locally advanced muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC; ie, T3-4 or node positive) have suboptimal outcomes with neoadjuvant therapy followed by radical cystectomy or trimodal therapy. This phase 2 trial evaluated a bladder-sparing strategy combining neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) plus tislelizumab followed by radiotherapy for patients with locally advanced MIBC who were considered nonideal candidates for bladder preservation (ChiCTR2100045213). Patients with cT2-4bN0-3M0-1a MIBC received 3-4 cycles of gemcitabine plus cisplatin/carboplatin with tislelizumab. Those without progression received radiotherapy, with tislelizumab continued for up to 1 yr. The primary endpoint was the post-radiotherapy clinical complete response (cCR) rate; secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), bladder-intact disease-free survival (BI-DFS), overall survival (OS), and toxicity. This study enrolled 45 patients (the intention-to-treat [ITT] population). The initial cCR rate was 51.1%, and the objective response rate was 80.0% after neoadjuvant therapy. Of the 36 patients who completed radiotherapy (the per-protocol [PP] population), 34 achieved cCR.This yielded a cCR rate of 75.6% (95% confidence interval [CI] 61.3-85.8) for the ITT population and 94.4% (95% CI 81.9-98.5) for the PP population. With a median follow-up of 48.8 mo, no patient underwent salvage surgery after radiotherapy. The 4-yr ITT PFS, BI-DFS, and OS rates were 66.2% (95% CI 53.0-82.6), 64.0% (95% CI 50.7-80.7), and 72.1% (95% CI 59.2-87.9), respectively; PP rates were 74.1% (95% CI 60.0-91.6) for PFS and BI-DFS, and 82.0% (95% CI 68.7-97.8) for OS. This combined modality approach-integrating NAC, tislelizumab, and radiotherapy-showed promising clinical activity with acceptable toxicity in selected patients with locally advanced MIBC.

papers.abstract: RNA-defined R-loop-associated malignant-cell states and their chromatin correlates in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remain incompletely characterized. We integrated GSE207493 and GSE264586 single-cell RNA-sequencing data and calculated a frozen 18-gene R-loop-associated score from raw counts after CPM normalization and log2(CPM+1) transformation. Patient-level models assessed transcriptional associations, while patient-matched scATAC-seq was analyzed using pseudobulk, chromVAR and RNA-ATAC concordance analyses. Dataset-specific and pooled scTenifoldKnk models prioritized NCL for cellular validation. Twelve of 25 prespecified transcriptional programs were associated with the continuous patient-level score at BH q < 0.05, encompassing immune, DNA-repair, metabolic and hypoxic features. scATAC-seq identified 10,800 differentially accessible peaks, including 221 retained by patient-blocked sensitivity analysis, with positive RNA-ATAC effect concordance after excluding score and transfer features. NCL was the only candidate ranked within the top quartile in both dataset-specific networks and all three pooled models, with highly concordant pooled perturbation profiles and Hallmark enrichments. NCL depletion increased RNase H-sensitive S9.6 signals and γ-H2AX, reduced antigen-presentation markers and increased checkpoint markers. NCL re-expression and RNase H1 overexpression partially restored γ-H2AX and marker expression in 786-O cells; RNase H1 overexpression also reduced S9.6 signals. Marker changes were concordant in 769-P cells. The RNA-derived score defines a ccRCC malignant-cell state with coordinated transcriptional and chromatin-accessibility remodeling. NCL perturbation and RNase H1 intervention support an NCL-dependent, RNase H-sensitive link to DNA damage and antigen-presentation/checkpoint remodeling.

papers.abstract: The perivascular space (PVS) mediates cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-dependent central nervous system (CNS) immune surveillance, yet its role in brain malignancies remains unclear. Here, we show that PVS serves as a conduit for CSF-derived CD8+ T cells that participate in antitumor immunity. In glioma patients, impaired PVS fluid dynamics is associated with worse outcomes. Pathologically, excessive collagen deposition in PVS impedes T cell infiltration and promotes T cell exhaustion. In murine brain tumor models, a safe dose of CSF-delivered collagenase degrades PVS collagen, enhances T cell infiltration, reduces exhaustion, and synergizes with anti-PD1 therapy. Mechanistically, tumor-associated CSF acidosis in PVS activates stromal cells via pH-sensing receptors to overproduce collagen. Targeting these receptors or neutralizing acidosis normalizes PVS collagen, restores T cell function, and improves survival. Our findings identify PVS as an important route for T cell entry and demonstrate that reversing PVS dysfunction restores immune cell trafficking and enhances antitumor immunity.

papers.abstract: Overexpression of leucine-rich repeat-containing protein 15 (LRRC15) is closely linked to cancer progression and rheumatoid arthritis (RA), making it a promising therapeutic target. Conventional single-target approaches suffer from limited efficacy and off-target effects. Here, we develop a dual-targeting nanoplatform based on Ag2S@ZIF-8 nanoparticles (NPs) and modified with hyaluronic acid (HA) for imaging-guided photothermal-gene editing synergistic therapy against LRRC15-related diseases. The resulting Ag2S-crRNA/Cas12a@ZIF-8@HA (ACZH) NPs deliver CRISPR RNA (crRNA) for sequence-specific LRRC15 recognition, together with HSP70 promoter-driven Cas12a plasmids. Ag2S NPs enable real-time NIR-II fluorescence imaging and generate localized hyperthermia (>42°C) that activates the HSP70 promoter to induce Cas12a expression and subsequent LRRC15 editing. In breast and lung cancer xenograft models, ACZH NPs achieve tumor inhibition rates of 81.37% and 82.5%, respectively; in an RA model, they reduce joint inflammation, prevent cartilage erosion, and promote bone repair. These findings offer a safe and effective strategy for LRRC15-related diseases.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) primarily targets dysfunctional T cells but is limited by insufficient effector infiltration, highlighting upstream priming constraints. Human colorectal cancer analyses reveal suppression of dendritic cell (DC)-associated antigen-presentation programs. We identify T cell immunoglobulin and mucin-domain containing-3 (TIM-3) and cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4) as a two-tier checkpoint module across the DC-T cell axis that restricts cDC innate activation and T cell co-stimulation, respectively. To overcome this barrier, we establish programmable TIM-3/CTLA-4 aptamer-based DC-T cell engagers (DCEs) as a proof of concept and develop a bispecific antibody (BsAb) integrating dual blockade with enhanced DC-T engagement. DCEs promote cDC migration to tumor-draining lymph nodes, sustain intratumoral cytotoxic T cell responses through the CXCL16-CXCR6 axis, and establish durable antitumor memory in murine models. Tumor-cell pyroptosis and oxaliplatin enhance DCE activity. A human TIM-3/CTLA-4 BsAb promotes autologous DC-T engagement, T cell priming, and cytotoxic function. These findings identify the antigen-presentation interface as a targetable checkpoint axis and support TIM-3/CTLA-4 DCEs as a translational cancer immunotherapy strategy.

papers.abstract: Chemotherapy is undermined by drug resistance and inadequate antitumor immunity, yet the metabolic mechanism that coordinates these two processes remains unclear. Here, we show that chemotherapy-induced depletion of uridine monophosphate (UMP) promotes chemoresistance by suppressing B cell immunity and enhancing tumor glycolysis. Mechanistically, UMP is imported into B cells via solute carrier family 28 member 2, activating adenosine kinase-dependent tyrosine-protein kinase SYK phosphorylation to promote plasma cell differentiation and enhance CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity. In tumor cells, UMP allosterically inhibits the histone acetyltransferase KAT5, thereby reducing histone H4 acetylation and glycolytic gene transcription. However, chemotherapy activates mitogen-activated protein kinase 8 to phosphorylate uridine-cytidine kinase 1 at serine 11, disrupting UMP synthesis and relieving KAT5 inhibition. Pharmacological UMP supplementation restores chemosensitivity in murine models. Clinically, circulating UMP correlates with better therapeutic responses and prolonged survival. These findings highlight UMP as a metabolic modulator and a potential biomarker for evaluating chemotherapy response.

papers.abstract: Preoperative serum albumin is widely used to stratify surgical risk and is often reduced to a single threshold, yet it is a negative acute-phase reactant that reports on inflammation, illness burden, and physiologic reserve rather than nutritional intake. The same value therefore need not carry the same prognostic meaning in every patient. Chronic preoperative opioid exposure defines one such context, but risk models treat albumin and opioid exposure as independent predictors and have not tested whether opioid exposure changes what an albumin value indicates. We analyzed the All of Us Research Program Controlled Tier Curated Data Repository v9. Adults aged 18 years or older with a first inpatient surgical procedure and a serum albumin in the 90 days before surgery were eligible. Opioid exposure in the preceding year was classified as chronic (at least three fills or at least 90 cumulative days' supply), some (one to two fills with fewer than 90 days' supply), or naive. The outcome was 30-day all-cause inpatient readmission, anchored to the index discharge date. Logistic regression modeled readmission on albumin centered at 4.0 g/dL, chronic opioid exposure, and their interaction, adjusted for age, female sex, and Elixhauser comorbidity count. The albumin window was varied from 30 to 365 days. The cohort comprised 42,239 adults (23,032 opioid-naive, 6811 some-opioid exposure, 12,396 chronic), of whom 7798 of 42,239 (18.5%) were readmitted within 30 days. Albumin was not associated with readmission among nonchronic participants (odds ratio, 1.03 per 1 g/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.98-1.09), nor was chronic opioid exposure at an albumin of 4.0 g/dL (odds ratio, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.97-1.09). The albumin × chronic-opioid interaction odds ratio was 0.738 (95% CI, 0.681-0.800), P < 0.001, indicating that higher albumin was associated with lower readmission odds specifically among chronic opioid users. On the harm scale, hypoalbuminemia (below 3.5 g/dL) interacted with chronic exposure in the same direction (odds ratio, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.13-1.43). The interaction held across all five albumin windows. Chronic preoperative opioid exposure modified the association between preoperative serum albumin and 30-day readmission, such that low albumin marked elevated readmission risk in chronic opioid users but not in other patients. This is statistical effect modification in observational data, not evidence of causation. It supports reading albumin in the context of opioid exposure rather than adopting a new or opioid-specific albumin threshold, which this study does not propose.

papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is common in older adults undergoing hip surgery. Noise exposure is associated with increased delirium risk. We hypothesized that perioperative noise isolation would reduce POD in these patients. In this single-center, randomized, patient- and assessor-blind trial, 320 patients (aged ≥65 y) undergoing hip surgery under sevoflurane anesthesia were randomly assigned 1:1 using block randomization stratified by age, surgery type, and planned surgical ICU admission to noise isolation (earmuffs from anesthesia induction to tracheal extubation before awakening) or control (routine care). The primary outcome was the incidence of POD during the first 7 postoperative days or until hospital discharge. Among 316 patients (mean age 78 y; 71.8% female) who completed the study (158 per group), POD occurred in 19 (12.0%) patients in the noise isolation group vs. 36 (22.8%) in the control group (relative risk 0.53; 95% CI 0.32-0.88; P = 0.012). The absolute risk reduction was 10.8% (number needed to treat 9). The interventional effect remained significant after multivariable adjustment for stratification factors (adjusted odds ratio 0.42; 95% CI 0.23-0.80; P = 0.009) and after additional adjustment for Charlson Comorbidity Index (adjusted odds ratio 0.43; 95% CI 0.23-0.82; P = 0.010). Patients receiving noise isolation were less likely to experience moderate-to-severe pain and required less rescue analgesia. Perioperative noise isolation reduced the incidence of POD in older adults undergoing hip surgery. This simple, nonpharmacological intervention represents an immediately implementable strategy to enhance perioperative care. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400082211).

papers.abstract: Research from high-income countries indicates that perioperative care providers are at high risk for burnout, with potential downstream effects on patient safety. Adequate solutions to address burnout may be particularly important in low-income countries where the effects of burnout on staff motivation and migration are likely to be compounded by the current human resources crisis. This study aimed to explore solutions to address burnout among Rwandan perioperative care providers. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with perioperative care providers (obstetricians, surgeons, anesthetists, midwives, nurses) in hospitals across all five provinces in Rwanda. Interviews were analyzed using both inductive and deductive coding following standard procedures of thematic analysis. Interviews were completed with 61 participants from all levels of public hospitals (37% teaching, 6% referral, 52% district, and 5% unknown level). The participants identified solutions at multiple levels fitting within the multilevel model of burnout.At the individual level, many drew on internal values and self-developed coping mechanisms to manage occupational stress, emphasizing the importance of fulfilling basic needs such as sleep and nutrition, and stress-relief activities such as exercise and music. At the interpersonal level, support networks involving family, friends, religious communities, and colleagues played a significant role in sustaining resilience. At the hospital level, participants found motivation through positive patient outcomes. They underscored the impact of hospital organization on workload and recommended reducing inefficiencies.Regarding the healthcare system, concerns were raised about insufficient financial resources affecting staff salaries and access to essential medicines and equipment. Participants emphasized that increasing staffing levels would improve scheduling flexibility and reduce burnout. Finally, cultural factors such as recognition, appreciation, and respectful workplace interactions were deemed essential for morale. This study illustrates that resilience among healthcare professionals is shaped by a complex interplay of individual, interpersonal, institutional, and systemic factors. While many rely on personal values and coping strategies to manage the demands of clinical work, their resilience is often strained by unmet basic needs, geographic isolation, organizational inefficiencies, and broader systemic limitations such as inadequate staffing and financing. Cultural dynamics, including recognition, respect, and workplace relationships, further influence the capacity to cope with stress. To address burnout effectively, solutions must be adapted to the Rwandan context and implemented at all levels, ranging from promoting self-care and peer support to improving hospital management and resource allocation, and to promoting innovative and evidence-based interventions.

papers.abstract: The gut microbiota can profoundly influence the efficacy of treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), but the impact of bacteria residing within lung tumors remains largely unexplored. In this study, we show that bacteria colonizing mouse lung metastases hinder antitumor immunity by promoting regulatory T-cell (Treg) differentiation and function through metabolites, including valine. Antibiotic inhalation, a strategy to achieve high airway concentration with limited effects on the gut microbiota, reduced Treg frequencies, expanded stem-like T cells, broadened the T-cell receptor repertoire, and boosted complete remission rates following programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade. Replacing tumor-associated bacteria, transplanting Tregs, or depleting T cells dampened the efficacy of the anti-PD-1/antibiotics combination, whereas the adoptive transfer of T cells from combination-treated mice into naïve mice conferred protection against tumor challenge. DNA sequences consistent with tumor-associated bacteria in mouse metastases were detected in 33 of 95 human lung cancer specimens, which exhibited increased Treg and reduced T-cell infiltration. Our findings reveal that tumor-associated microbes represent a barrier to ICI therapy that can be removed by disrupting intratumoral bacterial dysregulation with aerosolized antibiotics. Tumor-associated bacteria promote intratumoral Treg accumulation, limiting PD-1 blockade efficacy, and inhaled antibiotics break this immunosuppressive axis, thereby boosting T-cell control of lung metastasis upon checkpoint blockade.

papers.abstract: Interleukin-2 (IL-2) is critical for sustaining T-cell expansion during infection and cancer. However, the α subunit of the high-affinity IL-2 receptor (IL-2Rα, also known as CD25) is only transiently expressed following activation, limiting durable cytokine responsiveness. To overcome this barrier, we engineered CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells with constitutive IL-2Rα expression and evaluated their functional fitness. CAR19-IL-2Rα T cells exhibited hypersensitive STAT5 signaling and proliferated more robustly than conventional CAR19 T cells under limiting IL-2 conditions. In long-term rechallenge assays, enforced IL-2Rα expression sustained proliferation, enhanced tumor clearance, and conferred resistance to regulatory T cell (Treg)-mediated suppression by improving competition for IL-2. In a xenograft B cell lymphoma model, CAR19-IL-2Rα T cells improved tumor control and survival without increasing circulating cytokine levels associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS) or the expression of exhaustion-associated markers PD1 and LAG3. Transcriptomic profiling revealed strong induction of DDIT4, an mTORC1 inhibitor, following constitutive IL-2Rα expression in vivo, suggesting the activation of a feedback mechanism that limits CAR T-cell expansion. Together, these results identify IL-2Rα overexpression as an engineering strategy that enhances CAR T-cell function, improves resistance to Treg-mediated immunosuppression, and promotes durable antitumor activity. This work establishes cytokine receptor rewiring as a simple and clinically compatible approach to enhance CAR T-cell therapy in B-cell malignancies.

papers.abstract: CAR-T cell therapy has transformed clinical outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, but its translation to breast cancer remains limited by antigen heterogeneity, on-target/off-tumor toxicity, poor tumor trafficking, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In this review, we provide a translational roadmap for CAR-based therapy in breast cancer, spanning target selection, therapeutic engineering, and clinical development. We performed a narrative targeted review of preclinical breast cancer models, clinical trials, conference abstracts, and registered CAR-based cellular therapy studies relevant to breast cancer, with evidence updated through 30 June 2026. The evidence was synthesized according to antigen selection, antigen density and safety, route of administration, engineering strategies, and biomarker-driven trial design. Preclinical models support the feasibility of CAR-based approaches in antigen-enriched settings, with activity reported against HER2, MUC1/MUC1*, ROR1, EGFR, c-MET, TROP2, B7-H3, Nectin-4, GD2, and mesothelin. Early clinical studies demonstrate that the administration is feasible with monitoring; however, objective responses remain uncommon, disease stabilization is the most frequent outcome, and clinically significant toxicities have occurred in selected programs. The most plausible near-term opportunities include HER2-positive disease with CNS or leptomeningeal involvement, antigen-enriched triple-negative breast cancer, and selected locoregional or high-antigen-density settings. Next-generation affinity-tuned, logic-gated, switchable, armored, and gene-edited platforms are being developed to improve tumor selectivity, trafficking, persistence, and resistance to immunosuppression. Overall, CAR-based therapy for breast cancer remains investigational, and future clinical trials should prospectively integrate quantitative target assessment, disease site, relevant biological and clinical barriers, manufacturing feasibility, and route of delivery to guide CAR-platform selection and correlative evaluation.

papers.abstract: Clinical outcomes for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remain dismal, with a 5-year survival rate of only 13%. Approximately 90% of PDAC harbor oncogenic KRAS mutations, and investigational (K)RAS inhibitors have demonstrated clinical promise. However, adaptive resistance limits overall response and durability, highlighting the need for deeper mechanistic insights and improved therapeutic strategies. Using temporal phosphoproteomic profiling, we identified Src family kinases (SFK) as a consistent and robustly upregulated signaling node following treatment with clinically-relevant (K)RAS inhibitors across KRAS-mutant cell-based and patient-derived PDAC models. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of SFK markedly enhanced the in vitro and in vivo efficacy of (K)RAS inhibitors in models refractory to (K)RAS-targeted therapy. SFK inhibition led to suppression of the YAP signaling axis, providing a potential mechanism for the observed therapeutic cooperativity. Collectively, these findings implicate SFK as an important driver of adaptive resistance to (K)RAS inhibition and support co-targeting SFK and KRAS as a promising therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract: Oncogenic KRAS drives pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Although RAS antagonists can induce initial therapeutic responses, the rapid emergence of resistance limits benefit. To define therapeutic response and resistance mechanisms, we deployed two complementary preclinical PDAC models, including a degron-regulated KRASG12D-dependent transplantation model and a KrasG12V-driven PDAC mouse model treated with the RAS(ON) multiselective inhibitor, RMC-7977. KRASG12D degradation provoked RAS-dependent relapse, characterized by compensatory wild-type (WT) RAS upregulation, restored MAPK signaling and proliferation, and a shift toward hybrid cancer cell states. In contrast, RMC-7977 treatment triggered rapid RAS-independent resistance within 7 days, distinguished by suppressed MAPK activity yet restored proliferation with increased epithelial differentiation, and upregulation of FYN. Mechanistically, this RAS-independent program converged on a SRC family kinase (SFK)-YAP axis. Antagonism of WT RAS or FYN attenuated resistance, and combining FYN/SFK antagonism with RMC-7977 prevented the uncoupling of MAPK signaling from cell proliferation in the KrasG12V PDAC model. These findings identify distinct RAS-dependent versus -independent adaptive pathways orchestrating resistance to RAS inhibition in PDAC and propose combination strategies for clinical evaluation to enhance the durability of KRAS-directed therapy. Divergent programs, mediated by protooncogenic wild-type RAS or an FYN/SFK-YAP axis, drive resistance to KRASG12D degradation and RMC-7977 in pancreatic cancer, revealing targetable vulnerabilities that prolong survival and inform durable therapies. See related article by Lin et al., p. XX .
