papers.abstract: Glioblastoma and other malignant brain tumors are difficult to treat due to the invasive behavior of the disease, resistance to conventional medicines, and the blood-brain barrier that limits delivery of therapeutics. This systematic review evaluates the potential of Sonodynamic Therapy (SDT), a non-invasive therapy that combines low-intensity ultrasound with tumor-selective sonosensitizers to produce fatal reactive oxygen species (ROS). A comprehensive literature search was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Analysis of 36 qualifying studies suggested that SDT could induce tumor-specific apoptosis and necrosis with little injury to healthy brain tissue by generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) and ultrasonic cavitation. Various sonosensitizers, such as 5-aminolevulinic acid, Photofrin II, and novel nanosonosensitizers, can improve their tumor targeting and efficacy. Early-phase clinical trials, including phase 0/1, phase 1 and phase 1/2 trials, have demonstrated encouraging safety, feasibility, and preliminary biological and clinical activity in high-grade gliomas and juvenile brain tumors. Optimization of the ultrasonic parameters (frequency, intensity, pulse patterns) is critical for therapeutic outcomes. Moreover, novel combination approaches with chemotherapy, radiation, and immunotherapy may synergistically improve the anti-tumor advantages of SDT. To summarize, SDT is a novel and minimally invasive therapy that has the potential to significantly improve the outcomes of patients with malignant brain tumors by selectively targeting tumor cells. Although the clinical application is enabled by improvements in sonosensitizer design and ultrasound technology, some problems with standardization of protocols and optimization of delivery still exist. Larger clinical trials are needed to confirm its efficacy and safety and its integration with multimodal therapy may delineate future neuro-oncological treatment paradigms.

papers.abstract: Malignant hyperthermia national incidence and mortality in the United States have not been estimated for the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision period. Diagnosis codes cannot separate an acute event from susceptibility, and previous chart review found only about one in four coded cases were true events. The authors estimated incidence and mortality using intravenous dantrolene as a coding-validity instrument. This retrospective cohort study used Epic (USA) Cosmos, a de-identified multi-institutional dataset, greater than 2016 through 2024. Malignant hyperthermia was identified by International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision-Clinical Modification code T88.3. The primary definition matched the only previous U.S. national study (billing final, any listed, mimics excluded). Rates per million used a fixed panel of 201 hospitals contributing inpatient discharges every year, with trend tested by Cochran-Armitage test. Coding positive predictive value (PPV) was assessed by anchoring the diagnosis to inpatient intravenous dantrolene. Incidence was stable at approximately seven per million discharges (pooled, 7.3; 95% CI, 6.7 to 7.9) with no significant trend (P = 0.086), roughly half the most recent published estimate (13.3 per million, 2005). The treatment-anchored PPV was 24.3% (95% CI, 21.3 to 27.5), reproducing the chart-validated 23.4%. A 94% rise in broadly coded cases in 2024 attenuated at the primary definition (+9%) and was absent among treatment-anchored events (PPV, 14.6%). In-hospital mortality was 5.0% (95% CI, 3.7 to 6.8). Present-on-admission comorbidity burden was the only independent predictor of death (odds ratio, 1.08 per diagnosis; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.12). In this large health system network, malignant hyperthermia incidence was approximately seven per million inpatient discharges and stable, with in-hospital mortality of 5.0%. Diagnosis coding overstates the condition. Anchoring to intravenous dantrolene reproduces the chart-validated PPV and yields a treatment-confirmed incidence of approximately 1.7 per million. The anchored estimate is robust to the coding inflation observed in 2024.

papers.abstract: The impact of depressive symptoms on treatment efficacy among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) who are receiving first-line immunotherapy remains uncertain. This prospective cohort analysis enrolled patients diagnosed with HCC at BCLC Stage B or C, who initiated first-line immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapy at a single center in China between January 1, 2023, and August 31, 2024. Depressive symptoms at baseline were evaluated using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9, with depressive symptoms defined as PHQ-9 ≥ 5, reflecting at least mild depressive symptoms. The primary endpoint of the study was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints comprised overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), and quality of life (QoL). Treatment regimens were heterogeneous. To estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for the survival outcomes, Cox proportional hazards regression models were utilized, both before and after the application of propensity score matching. Of 200 patients included, 120 (60%) had baseline depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 ≥ 5), and 182 patients (91.0%) received concomitant targeted therapy. Median follow-up was 31.0 months (95% CI, 30.0-34.0). Patients with depressive symptoms had significantly shorter median PFS than those without (3.0 vs 6.0 months; adjusted HR, 1.87; 95% CI, 1.31-2.66). Median OS was also shorter in patients with depressive symptoms (13.0 vs 22.5 months; adjusted HR, 3.00; 95% CI, 1.96-4.59). Depressive symptoms were also associated with lower ORR (adjusted OR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.13-0.57) and persistently worse QoL during treatment. Baseline depressive symptoms were associated with poorer survival, reduced treatment response, and worse QoL in patients with advanced HCC receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy. These findings support the need for further studies to determine whether systematic psychological assessment and intervention can improve clinical and patient-reported outcomes in this population.

papers.abstract: ESR1 mutations commonly emerge on endocrine therapy (ET) during breast cancer treatment and contribute to therapeutic resistance. However, the impact of increasing degrees of polyclonality is not well understood. We conducted a retrospective, descriptive review of patients with estrogen receptor-positive (ER + ) metastatic breast cancer (MBC) and ≥10 concurrent ESR1 variants defined as extreme ESR1 polyclonality, assessed on circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) between August, 2020 and July, 2025. Patient and tumor characteristics, frequency of ESR1 variants, co-occurring mutations, and clonal changes in ESR1 in response to treatment were explored. Nine patients met criteria for extreme ESR1 polyclonality. Patients received a median of 1 line of ET in the metastatic setting before their initial ctDNA assessment, which identified 0-31 ESR1 clones (mean, 6). The most frequent ESR1 clonal mutations were Y537N, Y537S, and D538G. Common co-alterations included TP53 and RB1 mutations and CCND1 amplification. Tumor mutational burden (TMB) at the time extreme ESR1 polyclonality emerged ranged from 6.7-56.5 mutations per megabase (mut/Mb); all assessable tumors were microsatellite stable (MSS). This represents the first case series to explore extreme ESR1 polyclonality. Characterizing the mutational dynamics associated with this phenomenon may improve understanding of ESR1 mutations and related impacts on treatment resistance.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting PD-1/PD-L1 have transformed the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer, yet their clinical benefit remains limited even among patients with PD-L1-positive tumours, highlighting the need for improved predictive biomarkers. Although PD-L1 is heavily N-glycosylated, whether site-specific glycoform heterogeneity regulates therapeutic antibody binding and contributes to clinical outcome remains unclear. We applied a site-resolved glycoproteomic platform to characterise PD-L1 N-glycan heterogeneity in lung cancer cell lines and archived formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tumours from patients treated with atezolizumab monotherapy. Structural modelling, functional assays, and tumour analyses were used to assess the mechanistic and clinical relevance of defined glycoforms. We identified poly-N-acetyllactosamine (poly-LacNAc) elongation at Asn200 of PD-L1 as a glycoform feature associated with reduced atezolizumab binding. Structural modelling indicated that extended N200 glycans can approach and partially occlude the antibody-binding interface, supporting a steric basis for impaired binding. Clinically, PD-L1 immunohistochemistry alone had limited value for progression-free survival stratification, whereas stratification based on PD-L1-associated poly-LacNAc revealed significant outcome differences. Patients with poly-LacNAc-positive PD-L1 had markedly shorter progression-free survival than those without this feature. Site-specific PD-L1 glycosylation determines therapeutic antibody binding and represents a clinically relevant layer of immune checkpoint regulation in lung cancer.

papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a gynecologic malignancy characterized by substantial incidence and mortality. Angiogenesis is a central driver of OC progression and therapeutic resistance; however, clinically relevant angiogenesis-focused biomarkers that incorporate features of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain inadequately defined. An exploratory 14-gene prognostic signature was developed and evaluated using transcriptomic and survival data from the TCGA-OV cohort with angiogenesis-related genes derived from the GO database. Functional enrichment and immune infiltration analyses were performed to characterize biological differences between risk groups. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were further interrogated to delineate cell type-specific expression patterns. Candidate genes were validated in OC cell lines using RT-qPCR, Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and functional assays. Angiogenesis-related features effectively stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly different overall survival (OS) outcomes. High-risk tumors displayed coordinated activation of angiogenesis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and inflammatory pathways, accompanied by a distinct immune remodeling profile. Integrative transcriptomic profiling and literature review highlighted clusterin (CLU) and ceruloplasmin (CP) as candidate mediators associated with angiogenesis-driven risk. Both genes were upregulated in OC tissues and cell lines, and their silencing significantly suppressed cell proliferation, migration, and EMT-associated marker expression. This study establishes an exploratory angiogenesis-centered prognostic framework for OC and identifies CLU and CP as candidate mediators associated with progression-related cellular phenotypes in vitro. These findings highlight the biological relevance of CLU and CP in angiogenesis-associated phenotypes and provide insights into vascular-immune features of OC.

papers.abstract: Regulatory T (Treg) cells contribute to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICIs) resistance in cancer, yet a systematic approach to capture their pan-cancer impact on treatment outcomes remains limited. We analyzed scRNA-seq data from ICI-treated patients to characterize Treg-related features, including patient-level Treg proportions and exploratory intra-Treg CIBERSORTx scores. Treg.Sig, a pan-cancer Treg-associated immune-microenvironmental signature, was then derived from pre-annotated Treg cells across 32 scRNA-seq datasets and further evaluated by patient-level pseudobulk sensitivity analyses. The signature's association with immunosuppression, intratumor heterogeneity (ITH), and total mutation burden (TMB) was assessed in the TCGA pan-cancer cohort. Building upon this signature, we applied and systematically compared seven machine learning and four deep learning algorithms across 10 ICIs-treated RNA-Seq cohorts to identify the optimal predictive model. Finally, 29 CRISPR datasets were analyzed to prioritize resistance-associated targets, with candidate genes validated by immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blot. Exploratory cell-level analyses showed lower intra-Treg CIBERSORTx scores in responders in both cohorts. In SKCM, patient-level analysis showed a higher Treg/CD4 T-cell proportion in non-responders, whereas broader Treg proportions did not differ by response. Treg.Sig was positively correlated with markers of immunosuppression, ITH, and TMB. The optimal Treg.Sig model achieved area under the receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curves (AUCs) of 0.74 and 0.72 in validation and test sets, respectively, and 0.61-0.87 in independent test sets, outperforming existing transcriptomic models in predicting ICIs response. Among Treg.Sig genes, five immune resistance-related genes were identified through CRISPR data; LYZ and C1QA were significantly downregulated in ICIs responders, as confirmed by multiple experimental approaches. We developed a pan-cancer Treg-associated immune-microenvironmental signature and, through systematic application of multiple machine-learning and deep-learning algorithms, established a predictive model for ICI-response stratification. These findings support the potential utility of Treg.Sig for treatment-response stratification and highlight candidate genes for further investigation in Treg-associated immune resistance.

papers.abstract: Bioelectric signalling arises from the coordinated activity of ion channels, transporters, exchangers, and pumps, which establish the membrane potential and ionic gradients, generate endogenous electric fields, and support intercellular bioelectric coupling. These occur in both excitable and non-excitable tissues, where they interact with biochemical, mechanical, metabolic, and transcriptional networks. Excitable tissues serve as established model systems linking ion transport to rapid bioelectric activity and organ function. This review focuses primarily on the less extensively characterised roles of persistent and spatially organised bioelectric states in non-excitable and weakly excitable tissues. Evidence from the fields of development, regeneration, wound repair, immunity, and tissue remodelling suggests that bioelectric states may function as instructive signals, modulators of signalling responsiveness, permissive physiological conditions, or integrated indicators of cell and tissue state. This functional classification provides a framework for interpreting bioelectric alterations associated with cancer, fibrosis, chronic inflammation, metabolic disease, and neurological and cardiovascular disorders. We examine how membrane voltage, calcium signalling, endogenous electric fields, and gap junctional coupling interact with canonical pathways and tissue architecture. Experimental criteria are proposed to distinguish regulatory mechanisms from adaptive or secondary changes. The development of bioelectric diagnostics is evaluated in relation to analytical validity, biological interpretation, clinical validity, and clinical utility, together with therapeutic strategies based on ion channel modulation, electrical stimulation, conductive biomaterials, and bioelectronic interfaces. Integrating quantitative measurements, controlled perturbations, and computational modelling could help define when bioelectric states offer mechanistic leverage, predictive information, or clinically actionable targets.

papers.abstract: Grade IV glioma remains highly lethal, and effective therapies for recurrent disease remain limited. Glioma stem cells (GSCs) contribute to therapeutic resistance and tumor recurrence, providing a rationale for GSC-targeted immunotherapy. We conducted a single-center, single-arm investigator-initiated trial evaluating locoregional administration of CD44/CD133 bispecific chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells incorporating a truncated interleukin-7 receptor α (IL-7Rα) intracellular domain in ten adults with recurrent grade IV glioma. Treatment was well tolerated, with no dose-limiting toxicities or Grade ≥2 cytokine release syndrome. Adverse events were predominantly mild and transient, and no patient required IL-6 or IL-1 blockade. CAR-T cell leakage into peripheral blood remained minimal, whereas cerebrospinal fluid cytokine elevations were modest following infusion. Three patients achieved partial responses. The median overall survival after the first CAR-T cell infusion was 465 days. Exploratory single-cell RNA sequencing and proteomic analyses suggested patient stratification in macrophage-associated signatures, particularly in interferon signaling and antigen-presentation programs, which were associated with distinct clinical outcomes independently of IDH mutation status in this cohort. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and safety of repeated locoregional administration of GSC-targeting IL-7Rα-armored bispecific CAR-T cells. Exploratory immune profiling further identified inter-patient heterogeneity in macrophage-associated immune programs, which warrants validation in larger prospective studies. (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05577091, NMPA No. CXSL2500032).

papers.abstract: The application process for a complex general surgical oncology (CGSO) fellowship relies heavily on in-person interviews. Applicants incur significant financial and logistical costs, which have not been formally assessed. A cross-sectional survey of the 2025 CGSO applicant cohort was conducted. The survey tool assessed preferences regarding in-person versus virtual interviews as well as overall financial and opportunity costs incurred via the in-person interview process. Financial toxicity was evaluated using a modified 9-item FACIT-COST tool. Participants were recruited via direct outreach. Survey results were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Of 87 subjects contacted, 36 (41.4%) participated in the survey. The applicants applied to a median of 31.5 programs, ultimately attending 13 interviews. The median total cost incurred by the applicants was $7736. Transportation ($3850) and lodging ($2000) represented the largest expenses. The applicants estimated per-interview costs of $850 when travel to a different city was required. More than half of the applicants (55.6%) had to use savings or retirement funds, estimating a mean 21.4% reduction in savings. The median modified FACIT-COST score was 25.7, indicating incurred financial toxicity. The applicants missed a median of 18 clinical days. The majority (88.9%, n = 32) of the participants reported a preference for in-person over virtual interviews. Applicants for a CGSO fellowship personally incur significant financial and logistical costs through the process of interviews. Despite these costs, most applicants prefer in-person over virtual interviews. These findings highlight a need to explore novel strategies to reduce the financial and logistical burden on applicants while maintaining the benefits of in-person interactions.

papers.abstract: Intraductal papillary mucinous carcinoma (IPMC) with lymph node (LN) metastasis exhibits aggressive behavior, yet its risk factors and subtype-specific outcomes remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify clinicopathologic predictors of LN metastasis and evaluate their prognostic impact. We retrospectively analyzed 152 patients who underwent curative resection for pathologically confirmed IPMC at a single tertiary center between 2007 and 2022. IPMC was defined as invasive carcinoma demonstrating histologic continuity with IPMN epithelium. Clinicopathologic factors were compared between LN-positive and LN-negative groups. LN metastasis was observed in 47 patients (30.9%) and was associated with significantly worse overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) (median OS: 24 versus 97 months; DFS: 11 versus 87 months; both p < 0.001). Invasive component size was significantly larger in the LN-positive group (36.7 versus 18.7 mm, p < 0.001). Multivariate analysis identified T stage ≥ 2 (OR 5.50, p = 0.005), extrapancreatic invasion (OR 8.47, p = 0.002), pancreatobiliary subtype (OR 4.81, p = 0.005), and gastric subtype (OR 4.07, p = 0.013) as independent predictors of LN metastasis. The gastric subtype demonstrated the highest rates of lymphovascular and venous invasion among all subtypes. LN metastasis is a strong prognostic factor in IPMC. Histological subtype, T stage, and extrapancreatic invasion should inform preoperative risk assessment, the thoroughness of nodal staging, and adjuvant therapy decisions. The aggressive invasive phenotype of the gastric subtype warrants particular attention.

papers.abstract: Analysis of 183 colorectal cancer (CRC) patient samples revealed that GSDME expression alone did not correlate with overall survival in chemotherapy-naive patients, but in those receiving chemotherapy, GSDME-positive tumors with low macrophage infiltration exhibited the greatest survival benefit. Motivated by these clinical observations, we investigated the crosstalk between GSDME-mediated pyroptosis and macrophage-driven immune suppression. Tumors with GSDME expression or undergoing GSDME-dependent pyroptosis release elevated levels of CCL2, which recruits and polarizes tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) toward the immunosuppressive phenotype. These immunosuppressive macrophages secrete TGF-β1, attenuating caspase-3-mediated GSDME cleavage, thereby forming a negative feedback loop that limits pyroptosis. Mechanistically, GSDME stabilizes CCL2 by suppressing its K48-linked ubiquitin-mediated degradation via USP48, while CCL2 binds GSDME at its caspase-3 cleavage-relevant site (D267), competitively inhibiting GSDME activation. Disruption of this GSDME-CCL2-TAMs axis through pharmacological inhibition of CCL2 with chondroitin sulfate or bindarit enhances pyroptosis, reduces TAM infiltration and immunosuppressive polarization, and synergizes with cisplatin to suppress tumor growth in vivo. Collectively, these findings reveal a dual and self-limiting role of GSDME-CCL2 crosstalk in tumor progression and highlight CCL2 blockade as a rational strategy to potentiate pyroptosis-based cancer therapy.

papers.abstract: The tumour microenvironment (TME) is a multidimensional dynamic and complex system of cells and non-cellular components that not only drives tumour progression but also substantially influences response to therapy. Understanding TME biology for basic research and identifying biomarkers in the TME to stratify patients for therapy is crucial for optimizing therapeutic outcomes. Current standards for investigating TME dynamics, if even considered beyond preclinical work, rely predominantly on samples for tissue staining and sequencing and require invasive procedures to obtain tissue via surgery or biopsies. This leads to limited assessment of spatial heterogeneity and minimal temporal information as this depends on the timing of tissue sampling, which results in undefined clinical utility. Molecular imaging provides promising solutions by enabling non-invasive, real-time multidimensional spatiotemporal probing of the TME that can complement current ex vivo practices. This Review highlights the relevance of molecular imaging agents and methods that can effectively capture spatiotemporal TME characteristics in situ, offering critical insights into tumour behaviour and treatment response. We provide an overview of current preclinical imaging strategies and their applications in identifying cellular and non-cellular components of the TME, along with monitoring progression-associated processes and treatment response. We showcase new developments and avenues being explored in preclinical imaging, as well as offer perspectives into existing and emerging clinical imaging of the TME to enhance patient care and highlight opportunities for improvement. Overall, integrating TME imaging into clinical practice holds the potential to bridge critical gaps in spatiotemporal resolution, ultimately enabling more precise diagnosis, patient stratification and personalized therapeutic interventions.

papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) engineering has transformed cellular immunotherapies, yet whether CAR signaling can direct innate lymphoid cell functions for therapeutic applications has not been established. IL-10-producing ILC2s (ILC210) suppress pathogenic T cell responses in preclinical transplant models, making them attractive candidates for engineered regulatory cell therapies. Here we show that CD28 and CD3z are endogenous signaling modules with distinct expression kinetics in ILC2 activation. We engineered human ILC210 with CARs incorporating these domains and demonstrate that CAR activation via CD3z, CD28 or both induces robust proliferation and cytokine production, with each domain inducing distinct transcriptional programs, and combined CD3z and CD28 signaling uniquely inducing cytotoxic programs. In a xenogeneic graft-versus-host disease model, CAR-ILC210 more effectively inhibited human T cell engraftment and activity, displayed enhanced persistence and trafficked to sites of T cell-mediated injury. These findings establish CAR-ILC2s as programmable cellular therapies, with CAR signaling architecture shaping distinct ILC2 effector programs.

papers.abstract: Caudal blockade is used widely in paediatric analgesia, but empirical data on the local anaesthetic dose-spread relationship remain limited. This study quantified craniocaudal spread dynamics of three ropivacaine concentrations using real-time magnetic resonance imaging. This prospective, observer-blinded trial allocated children undergoing elective surgery to receive caudal 0.2% ropivacaine at doses of 0.5 ml.kg-1, 1.0 ml.kg-1 or 1.5 ml.kg-1 (based on surgical requirements). Cranial spread was quantified using respiratory-gated 3 Tesla magnetic resonance imaging and assigned a vertebral level. Optic nerve sheath diameter was measured before and after block administration in children allocated to the high-dose group. Dose-spread relationships were assessed using linear regression. In total, data from 45 children (aged 1-3 y) were analysed. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed dose-dependent median (IQR [range]) spread was L2 (L2-L2 [L2-L1]) for 0.5 ml.kg-1; T12 (T12-T10 [L1-T10]) for 1.0 ml.kg-1; and T9 (T10-T9 [T10-T8]) for 1.5 ml.kg-1 (group differences H = 38.6, p < 0.001). Linear regression established that vertebral level = 5.8 + 5.3 × Dose (R2 = 0.79). Each 0.5 ml.kg-1 increment advanced spread by 3.1 levels (95%CI 2.6-3.6 levels). Dose correlated strongly with spread (Spearman's ρ = 0.87, p < 0.001), but not with age; weight; height; or scan time. No significant optic nerve sheath diameter changes occurred following the block. The magnetic resonance imaging-quantified dose-response model for caudal blockade showed a predictable linear cranial progression with a 0.2% ropivacaine dose of 1.5 ml.kg-1 safely achieving mid-thoracic coverage with no evidence of intracranial pressure elevation. The derived regression equation enables precise, personalised targeting of surgical sensory levels in children.

papers.abstract: Peri-operative respiratory adverse events are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in paediatric anaesthesia. Gaseous pollutants (such as ozone) and fine particles have direct effects on airways, and so exposure to pollutants may influence the risk of peri-operative respiratory adverse events. This prospective, observational cohort study aimed to examine how the incidence of peri-operative respiratory adverse events in children is influenced by pre-hospital exposure to air pollution. Data were collected prospectively at a tertiary paediatric centre in Western Australia over three data collection periods. Details of respiratory risk factors, anaesthesia management and the incidence of peri-operative respiratory adverse events (laryngospasm, bronchospasm, airway obstruction, severe coughing, desaturation, pulmonary aspiration and postoperative stridor) were recorded during anaesthesia induction, maintenance, emergence and recovery. Each patient's home suburb was used to determine exposure to air pollution in the 2 days before their procedure. This used data from the Department of Water and Environmental Regulation air quality monitoring stations across Western Australia. In this low-pollution Western Australian cohort of 7051 anaesthetic episodes involving 6754 individual patients undergoing general anaesthesia, short-term exposure to particulate and gaseous pollutants other than ozone was not associated with increased incidence of peri-operative respiratory adverse events. However, ozone exposure showed a borderline association with peri-operative respiratory adverse events, particularly in children with pre-existing respiratory disease. Ozone pollution showed a signal for increased peri-operative risk, despite generally low pollutant concentrations. The coastal meteorology of Perth, including the regular sea breeze known locally as the 'Fremantle Doctor', provides important context for the largely low pollutant concentrations observed even during times of significant wildfires. Regions with higher or more variable pollution may show stronger or clinically more important effects.

papers.abstract: Emergence from general anaesthesia is often accompanied by agitation, suggesting that recovery of consciousness can engage neural circuits that regulate arousal and behavioural responsiveness. The amygdala influences social, defensive, and exploratory behaviours, but whether orexinergic input to the amygdala regulates anaesthetic state transitions together with behavioural responses remains unclear. In male orexin-Cre mice, we combined viral tracing, electrophysiology, and RNAscope to define a lateral hypothalamic orexin (LHAOx) projection to the medial amygdala (MeA). Optogenetics, electroencephalography, electromyography, and fibre photometry were used to test how this circuit regulates arousal from isoflurane anaesthesia, as well as exploratory and place-preference behaviour. LHAOx neurones densely innervated the MeA, where orexin receptor 2 was more abundant than orexin receptor 1 (P<0.0001). Optogenetic activation of the LHAOx→MeA projection promoted arousal from 0.75 vol% isoflurane sedation (P<0.0001), delayed induction by 3 vol% isoflurane as measured by loss of the righting reflex (P=0.0074), and accelerated emergence from 2 vol% isoflurane as measured by return of the righting reflex (P=0.0098). In behavioural assays, activation of this projection suppressed open-field exploration, increased real-time place preference, and did not produce conditioned place preference. Activation of the LHAOx→MeA projection was accompanied by increased activity in MeA vesicular GABA transporter (MeAvGAT)-expressing neurones. Direct activation of MeAvGAT neurones replicated the arousal-promoting and reduced exploratory behaviour, whereas silencing their synaptic output eliminated the induction-delaying effect and shifted the real-time preference. The LHAOx projection to the MeA promotes anaesthetic arousal and acutely suppresses exploratory behaviour in male mice, with MeAvGAT serving as a key downstream target.

papers.abstract: Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine increasingly used for general anesthesia, but its effects on intraoperative evoked potential monitoring remain incompletely defined. This scoping review mapped the available clinical evidence on remimazolam-based anesthesia for intraoperative evoked potential monitoring. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and ProQuest were searched for studies reporting remimazolam use in surgical patients undergoing evoked potential monitoring. Seventeen studies were included, comprising randomized controlled trials, a dose-escalation study, an observational comparative study, a retrospective cohort study, case series, and case reports. Reported modalities included motor evoked potentials, somatosensory evoked potentials, and visual evoked potentials; no eligible study reported brainstem auditory evoked potentials. Overall, intraoperative evoked potential signals were successfully recorded under remimazolam-based anesthesia, with reproducible waveforms reported across modalities. Some comparative studies reported amplitudes or latencies comparable to, or more favorable than, those observed with propofol-based anesthesia. However, findings were inconsistent and limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous designs, variable dosing regimens, concomitant anesthetic use, and limited data on intraoperative movement, warning criteria, and diagnostic performance. Current evidence indicates that intraoperative evoked potential signals can be obtained under remimazolam-based anesthesia. However, the available evidence remains insufficient to establish the feasibility and reliability of remimazolam for intraoperative evoked potential monitoring, determine optimal dosing or monitoring-specific warning criteria, or demonstrate superiority over established anesthetic regimens.

papers.abstract: An increasing proportion of complex surgical procedures are being performed in the UK as day-cases, and NHS targets aim for these to encompass ≥ 75% of all surgeries. There has been limited outcome follow-up for this group of patients, particularly considering the prevalence of persistent postoperative opioid use and factors associated with its occurrence. Data from POPPY, a national, prospective, observational study exploring outcomes following day-case surgery in the UK, were used to estimate the prevalence of persistent postoperative opioid use at day 97 following surgery. Patient, anaesthetic and surgical factors associated with increased persistent postoperative opioid use were explored using multivariable analysis. Of the 7839 initially recruited patients, 3488 (44.5%) provided details of their analgesic medication at day 97 following surgery. The prevalence of daily persistent postoperative opioid use was estimated to be 11.8% (95%CI 11.1-13.2%). Patient factors associated with daily persistent postoperative opioid use were pre-operative opioid use; opioid use at day 7; and composite pain scores (day 1, day 3 and day 7). Compared with general surgery, ENT, breast and orthopaedic surgery carried a higher risk of persistent postoperative opioid use. Patient factors associated with a reduced odds ratio of persistent postoperative opioid use were: female sex; higher composite pain score at baseline; and Index of Multiple Deprivation quintile 4. Daily persistent postoperative opioid use at day 97 following surgery was associated with reduced quality of life scores. Daily persistent postoperative opioid use is common in the UK following day-case surgery. Patient and surgical factors that are associated with an increased risk of this outcome could be used to drive improvement in identification of at-risk patients pre-operatively and optimise postoperative prescribing pathways.

papers.abstract: Principles of effective antimicrobial stewardship include prescription of empiric therapy based on the most likely causative organism, with medication review within 72 h. Adherence to best practice in UK ICUs is unknown and the aim of this study was to evaluate patient- and unit-level antimicrobial use in UK ICUs. We conducted a prospective national audit of antimicrobial use in adults (aged ≥ 18 y) admitted to ICUs in the UK and Isle of Man with a point-prevalence survey. Subsequently, we collected longitudinal data on review of therapy and antimicrobial resistance in a subset of patients who had commenced therapy within the previous 3 days. We studied 2626 patients from 154/292 (52.7%) ICUs. Antimicrobial therapy was prescribed in 1592 (60.6%) patients. Of 2116 empiric antimicrobial orders, 1592 (75.2%) were compliant with unit-level guidelines. For non-compliant orders, 253 (12.0% of all empiric orders) were discussed with infection specialists and 69 (3.3%) provided justification for off-guidance therapy, but 202 (9.5%) were prescribed outside guidance without justification or discussion with infection specialists. Guideline-compliant review within 72 h of prescription took place in 1488/1606 (92.7%) eligible medication orders. A pre-specified stop or review date was strongly associated with antimicrobial review within 72 h (adjusted OR 9.3, 95%CI 5.4-16.2). We have benchmarked critical care antimicrobial stewardship and guideline compliance across the UK. We recommend that pre-specified review dates are added to all prescriptions, as the most important determinant of review identified in our audit. Future work should include national stewardship audit cycles to benchmark practice and inform quality improvement initiatives.

papers.abstract: Etomidate is commonly used for induction in hemodynamically unstable patients to preserve cardiovascular stability. However, concerns persist regarding potential adverse outcomes, including adrenal suppression and increased mortality. We evaluated whether intravenous anesthetic induction with etomidate was independently associated with adverse postoperative outcomes as compared to propofol induction. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 155,667 adult surgical patients undergoing induction with etomidate or propofol at our academic health system. Patients younger than 18 years of age, those receiving preoperative mechanical ventilation, and those with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status VI were excluded. The primary outcome was all-cause 30-day mortality; secondary outcomes included sepsis, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), cardiogenic shock, and acute kidney injury (AKI). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, comorbidity, physiologic, and surgical factors. Given substantial baseline imbalance between induction groups, propensity score matching (1:1) using the same covariates was performed. Sensitivity analyses included adjustment for neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, complete-case analyses, and interaction testing. A total of 155,667 patients met inclusion criteria, including 3846 (2.5%) who received etomidate and 151,821 (97.5%) who received propofol. Thirty-day mortality occurred in 1151 patients (0.74%). Unadjusted mortality was higher in the etomidate group (227/3846 [5.9%]) than in the propofol group (924/151,821 [0.61%]). After multivariable adjustment, etomidate use remained independently associated with increased 30-day mortality (aOR 1.44; 95% CI, 1.21-1.72; P < 0.001). Propensity score matching (n = 3832 per group) reduced the average standardized mean difference from 0.398 before matching to 0.023 after matching. The association persisted in the matched cohort (aOR 1.43; 95% CI, 1.14-1.78; P = 0.002), with observed mortality of 225/3832 (5.9%) among etomidate recipients and 157/3832 (4.1%) among propofol recipients, corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 1.8% and a number needed to harm of 56. In the matched cohort, etomidate was also associated with higher odds of sepsis (aOR 1.28; 95% CI, 1.08-1.52), acute coronary syndrome (aOR 1.24; 95% CI, 1.09-1.41), cardiogenic shock (aOR 1.56; 95% CI, 1.21-2.01), and acute kidney injury (aOR 1.27; 95% CI, 1.11-1.45). Post-induction hypotension was lower in the etomidate group (aOR 0.40, 95% CI 0.32-0.49; P < 0.001). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Etomidate induction was associated with increased 30-day mortality and major postoperative complications. Given the observational design, results should be interpreted with caution.

papers.abstract: The use of Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists (CRNAs) in medically directed anesthesia care teams has expanded, but the implications for anesthesia time and billing units remain uncertain, especially in relation to staffing supervision ratios (number of CRNAs to anesthesiologist). We conducted a retrospective fixed-panel observational study of unique surgical encounters spanning January 2018 through December 2024 using billing records from a large revenue cycle management company. The sample included encounters involving anesthesiologists, CRNAs, surgeons, and facilities across 47 states. We compared physician-alone cases with medically directed care-team cases using fixed-effects regression models. Outcomes included anesthesia minutes and anesthesia billing units (base, time, modifier, conditional, and total units). A Medicare subsample was analyzed for realized gross payments. Secondary analyses examined each encounter by the number of CRNAs the anesthesiologist medically directed simultaneously, that is, staffing ratios, to assess whether outcomes varied by level. Models adjusted for patient-, procedure-, surgeon-, facility-, and time-level factors. Care-team cases were associated with longer anesthesia time (adjusted difference +1.67 minutes; 95% CI, 1.11-2.23; P < .001) and higher total billing units (adjusted difference +0.11 units; 95% CI, 0.04-0.18; P = .003) than cases performed by an anesthesiologist alone. Both differences increased with the staffing ratio. Relative to physician-alone cases, anesthesia time was shorter with 1 CRNA directed (-2.52 minutes; 95% CI, -3.22 to -1.83), similar with 2 CRNAs (-0.13 minutes; 95% CI, -0.69 to 0.43), and longer with 3 CRNAs (+3.03 minutes; 95% CI, 2.40-3.66) and 4 CRNAs (+6.99 minutes; 95% CI, 6.18-7.80); total billing units followed the same pattern (1 CRNA, -0.23; 2 CRNAs, -0.02 [not significant]; 3 CRNAs, +0.21; 4 CRNAs, +0.50). In a Medicare subsample, gross payments differed little overall (-$3.53; 95% CI, -$5.13 to -$1.92) and followed the same staffing-ratio gradient (1 CRNA, -$10.44; 4 CRNAs, +$3.74). Medically directed CRNA care teams were associated with modestly longer anesthesia time and slightly greater billing-unit intensity than physician-alone care. These differences were small overall but increased with rising staffing ratios, indicating that the number of CRNAs directed concurrently is associated with measurable differences in anesthesia time and billing intensity.

papers.abstract: Intraoperative haemodynamic monitoring primarily targets arterial pressure and flow but might not adequately reflect tissue perfusion. The peripheral perfusion index provides a continuous, noninvasive, and readily available indicator of peripheral perfusion, but its prognostic significance across surgical populations remains uncertain. We hypothesised that greater intraoperative exposure to low perfusion index would be associated with postoperative complications and mortality. In this prespecified multicentre cohort study using electronic health record data, we included adults (≥18 yr) undergoing general anaesthesia for noncardiac surgery. The primary exposure was cumulative intraoperative area under a perfusion index of 1.5 expressed in PI⋅min. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. The secondary outcome was a 30-day composite of postoperative intensive care unit admission, reoperation, acute kidney injury, or prolonged hospital stay. Among 399 842 patients undergoing 540 101 procedures, a total of 7066 (1.3%) deaths occurred within 30 days: 654 (0.5%) among procedures with no exposure, 1185 (0.6%) in the lower half of exposed procedures, and 5227 (2.6%) in the upper half (split at 3.8 PI⋅min). Compared with no exposure, the adjusted odds ratio for 30-day mortality was 2.18 (95% CI 1.98-2.40, overall association P<0.001) at the 95th percentile of exposure (42.5 PI⋅min), with similar patterns observed across the major surgical specialties. For the composite outcome, the corresponding odds ratio was 1.16 (95% CI 1.14-1.18; P<0.001). Greater intraoperative exposure to low perfusion index was associated with higher postoperative mortality and complications in adult patients undergoing general anaesthesia for noncardiac surgery. papers.abstract: Electronic cigarette aerosols may promote airway inflammation, bronchial hyperreactivity, and impaired mucociliary defence, but their perioperative respiratory safety remains uncertain. We examined whether preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of postoperative respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence. We conducted a nationwide matched cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network database, comparing surgical patients with documented preoperative vaping-related disorder and cigarette nicotine dependence. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of postoperative respiratory complications, including pneumonia, respiratory failure, bronchospasm, noninvasive ventilation, and mechanical ventilation. Among 3817 matched pairs, preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of 30-day respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence (10.7% vs 5.1%, relative risk [RR] 2.11, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.79-2.49). Vaping-related disorder was also associated with increased risks of pneumonia (RR 3.20, 95% CI 2.40-4.28), respiratory failure (RR 2.48, 95% CI 1.98-3.10), bronchospasm (RR 1.92, 95% CI, 1.38-2.68), and noninvasive ventilation (RR 2.56, 95% CI 1.64-3.98). Vaping-related disorder combined with cigarette nicotine dependence was associated with a higher risk of respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence alone (RR 1.98, 95% CI 1.55-2.53), whereas vaping-related disorder alone showed a larger RR increase than neither diagnosis (RR 3.11, 95% CI 2.56-3.76). Among surgical patients, preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of postoperative respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence. These findings suggest that vaping history should be specifically assessed during preoperative evaluation and considered in perioperative respiratory risk stratification.

papers.abstract: Advanced age is a major risk factor for both delirium and dementia. A potential early biomarker for dementia is the brain-predicted age difference (brainPAD). We hypothesised that brain ageing accelerates after postoperative delirium (POD), and that increased brainPAD is associated with cognitive decline. Brain MRI scans were obtained in 287 older patients before and 3 months after major elective surgery, and two MRI scans at similar time intervals were obtained in 46 nonsurgical control participants. We computed grey matter brainPAD in patients with POD (POD+), patients without POD (POD-), and nonsurgical controls. The Trail Making Test (TMT) was administered at both time points to examine associations between changes in brainPAD and changes in attention/processing speed (TMT-A) and executive task switching (TMT-B and TMT B-A). Compared with the POD- group, brainPAD increased by an additional 6 (sd=3) months over time in the POD+ group (P=0.002). For each 1 year-over-year increase in brain age gap, patients took 2.3 s longer to complete the TMT-A (P=0.016), whereas no association was observed with TMT-B (P=0.254) or TMT B-A (P=0.91). Postoperativ edelirium is associated with accelerated brain ageing, which in turn is associated with decline in attention and processing speed. These findings help to understand the complex relationship between ageing, delirium, and dementia. NCT02265263.

papers.abstract: Postoperative complications remain a leading cause of mortality. Experimental data indicate that roxadustat, a first-in-class prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor, reduces ischaemia-reperfusion injury, accelerates wound healing, and enhances survival in sepsis. Therefore, preoperative administration of roxadustat might reduce perioperative organ injury. We examined the perioperative tolerability and the potential for adverse surgical interactions with roxadustat. In this phase 2a, single-centre, double-blind, randomised-controlled pilot trial, 150 patients undergoing major elective noncardiac surgery were allocated to preoperative roxadustat 100 mg or placebo for three alternate-day doses, with the last dose on the operative morning. The co-primary outcomes were preoperative adverse events and postoperative complications meeting standardised endpoint definitions within 30 days. Among 148 participants (52 [35.1%] females; median age 65 [range 24-84] yr) receiving at least one drug dose, at least one preoperative adverse event occurred in 21 of 75 (28%) in the roxadustat group and 20 of 73 (27%) in the placebo group (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.50-2.12). No serious adverse reactions occurred. Among 143 participants who proceeded to surgery (52 [36.4%] females; median age 65 [range 26-84] yr), ≥1 complication occurred in 23 of 74 participants (31%) who received roxadustat compared with 21 of 69 participants (30%) who received placebo (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.51-2.10). Days alive out of hospital within 30 days was similar between the groups. The annualised enrolment rate was 90 per year, with high levels of drug compliance. Preoperative roxadustat was feasible in patients having major surgery. Uncertainty remains regarding the safety and efficacy of this intervention. www.anzctr.org.au; ACTRN12624000188538.

papers.abstract: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the most common abdominal operation worldwide, yet whether opioid-free anaesthesia improves the overall analgesic benefit remains uncertain. In this multicentre randomised controlled trial, adults undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy were randomised 1:1 to receive opioid-free anaesthesia (dexmedetomidine, esketamine and sevoflurane) or opioid-inclusive anaesthesia (sufentanil and sevoflurane). Patients received prophylactic anti-emetics and multimodal analgesia with flurbiprofen axetil and ropivacaine wound infiltration. The primary outcome was the overall benefit of analgesia score (0-28, lower scores indicate greater benefit) at 24 h postoperatively; a 3-point difference was considered clinically relevant. Secondary outcomes included pain on movement at 24 h and chronic postsurgical pain at 90 days. Between March and September 2025, 315 patients completed this trial (158 opioid-free, 157 opioid-inclusive). The mean (SD) 24-h overall benefit of analgesia score was 2.2 (2.4) after opioid-free anaesthesia vs 3.4 (3.1) after opioid-inclusive anaesthesia (adjusted mean difference -1.3; 95%CI -1.8 to -0.8, p < 0.001), without reaching the threshold for clinical importance. Incidence of pain on movement (adjusted mean difference -0.2; 95%CI -0.4-0) and chronic postsurgical pain (16.1% vs 15.5%; adjusted relative risk 1.03; 95%CI 0.55-1.91) did not differ between groups. Opioid-free anaesthesia was associated with reduced intra-operative hypotension (19.6% vs 35.7%; relative risk 0.55; 95%CI 0.37-0.80) and lower incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (23.4% vs 33.8%; relative risk 0.69; 95%CI 0.48-0.98). Opioid-free anaesthesia did not achieve a clinically meaningful improvement in overall benefit of analgesia. These findings do not support its routine adoption in laparoscopic cholecystectomy. However, the observed reductions in intra-operative hypotension and postoperative nausea and vomiting suggest that this regimen may warrant consideration in selected patients, pending validation in future trials.

papers.abstract: It is common practice to convert an existing labour epidural into surgical anaesthesia for intrapartum caesarean delivery. However, this approach does not always provide adequate anaesthesia. This meta-analysis aimed to determine the incidence of inadequate anaesthesia during epidural conversion for intrapartum caesarean delivery. Databases were searched for observational studies and randomised controlled trials evaluating epidural conversion for intrapartum caesarean delivery. Using a random-effects model and the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation, we calculated the respective incidences of intra-operative patient-reported pain; use of supplemental analgesia; and conversion to general anaesthesia. A total of 43 studies, involving 11,904 patients, were included in the meta-analysis. Pooled incidences of intra-operative pain (eight studies), supplemental analgesia (34 studies) and conversion to general anaesthesia (33 studies) were 20.2% (95%CI 12.2-29.5%, I2 = 93.1%), 17.7% (95%CI 13.3-22.7%, I2 = 96.3%) and 1.3% (95%CI 0.7-2.1%, I2 = 81.7%), respectively. These results were consistent in sensitivity analyses and appeared unaffected by publication year, study design, country type, local anaesthetic used or use of epidural fentanyl. However, substantial heterogeneity was observed due to variability in study methodologies, measurement methods, definitions, thresholds and local clinical practices. This meta-analysis highlights the risk of inadequate anaesthesia and emphasises the importance of thorough pre-operative informed consent when converting labour epidurals to surgical anaesthesia for intrapartum caesarean delivery. However, the considerable heterogeneity in the pooled estimates indicates that these incidences vary significantly across different settings, suggesting that local audit data would be more informative for individual practices.

papers.abstract: The American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS) classification is widely used, but subjective interpretations cause evaluation variability. Although specific clinical examples were added in 2014 and 2020 to reduce ambiguity, their clinical adoption remains unclear. We evaluated awareness of these examples and whether a multifaceted educational intervention was associated with scoring consistency. This two-phase study evaluated ASA-PS scoring consistency. In Study 1, 45 anesthesiologists at two institutions evaluated 20 simulated adult, pediatric, and obstetric cases to assess understanding of official ASA-PS examples. In Study 2, a pre- and post-intervention study in clinical practice included 414 cases. The intervention included survey feedback, re-dissemination of official examples, and implementation of a reference system in the electronic medical record. The primary outcome was the exact agreement rate between clinician-assigned and consensus scores based on official examples. In Study 1, the overall correct rate with the official reference classifications was 47.6% (Cohen's kappa = 0.321). Correct rate was particularly low in pediatric cases (kappa = 0.243). Highly experienced anesthesiologists demonstrated lower correct rates and a tendency toward underestimation. In Study 2, the exact agreement rate increased from 73.5% before the intervention to 82.4% (OR 1.68, 95% CI 1.01-2.78) after the intervention. Cohen's kappa improved from 0.553 to 0.712, and underestimation decreased from 21.1% - 14.8%. Publishing clinical examples alone may be insufficient to standardize ASA-PS classification. A multifaceted intervention incorporating educational feedback and an electronic reference system was associated with improved scoring consistency.

papers.abstract: Palmitoylethanolamide (PEA), an endogenous lipid mediator, exhibits anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties, its efficacy as a stand-alone treatment for acute postoperative pain remains uncertain. This study compared oral micronized PEA with ibuprofen in managing pain following extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL). In this prospective, randomized, double-blind investigation, 120 patients classified as ASA I-II undergoing elective ESWL were evaluated. They were randomly divided to take either 600 mg of oral micronized PEA or 600 mg of ibuprofen two hours prior to the procedure, continuing every 12 h for 72 h. The primary endpoint was postoperative pain intensity quantified by visual analogue scale (VAS) 2 h post-ESWL. Secondary endpoints included VAS scores at predefined intervals, rescue analgesia, adverse events, and patient satisfaction. VAS scores were comparable between groups during the early postoperative period, including at 2 h (PEA: 1 [0-2] vs. ibuprofen: 1 [0-2], P = 0.091). However, pain was significantly higher with PEA at 12 h, 24 h, and 48 h (P < 0.001). Rescue analgesia was required more frequently with PEA (76.7% vs. 58.3%, P = 0.032), with greater cumulative opioid consumption (10.7 ± 2.2 vs. 9.4 ± 1.8 mg, P = 0.003). Gastrointestinal discomfort was more frequent with ibuprofen (21.7% vs. 1.7%, P < 0.001). In this active-comparator trial, oral micronized PEA was inferior to ibuprofen at 12-48 h after ESWL, with more rescue analgesia, but early pain scores were similar. The analgesic effect of PEA itself cannot be established. Fewer gastrointestinal adverse events warrant further study.

papers.abstract: Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) during total aortic arch replacement (TAR) is associated with coagulopathy. We investigated whether fresh frozen plasma (FFP) administration during CPB was associated with postoperative transfusion requirements and coagulation profiles after TAR. This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent elective TAR. Patients were categorized according to whether FFP was administered during CPB. The primary outcome was postoperative FFP transfusion from CPB separation to 12 h after intensive care unit admission. Secondary outcomes included perioperative plasma-derived product use, postoperative bleeding, re-exploration for bleeding, and serial coagulation parameters. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to adjust for potential confounders. Data from 156 patients were analyzed, including 111 patients in the Pre-FFP group and 45 in the Control group. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable, although deep hypothermic circulatory arrest duration and CPB fluid management differed between the groups. The adjusted mean difference in total post-CPB FFP transfusion units between the Pre-FFP and Control groups was - 1.54 units (95% confidence interval, - 7.51 to 4.43). No significant differences were observed in perioperative plasma-derived product use or bleeding outcomes. Although fibrinogen concentrations were higher and activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time-international normalized ratio were shorter at the end of CPB in the Pre-FFP group, these differences largely resolved after CPB. FFP administration during CPB was associated with transient improvement in coagulation parameters but was not associated with postoperative transfusion requirements or bleeding outcomes in adult patients undergoing elective TAR. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.abstract: We investigate the policy implications of statistically valid upper limits on anesthesia durations. We test whether these tolerance limits categorized by claims data (procedure, surgeon, and facility) differ in practical consequence from limits calculated with data pooled among surgeons and facilities. We evaluate whether using valid tolerance limits at typical insurer sample sizes would differ functionally from no limits. Simulations had 100,000 replicates per configuration with 8 surgeons per hospital: equal n = 10 or 300 cases per-surgeon or unequal (geometric) median n = 10 and 60. The within-surgeon coefficient of variation was 36.2%. The between-surgeon variance accounted for 22.4% of total log-time variance (intraclass correlation). Five tolerance-limit methods (pooled Weibull generalized pivotal quantity, pooled nonparametric, per-surgeon log-normal, per-surgeon 3-sigma, and per-surgeon nonparametric) were evaluated by coverage probability (95% was correct), case-volume-weighted percentage bias (0% best), functional quantile (90 th for 90 th percentile), and payment satisfaction (100% ideal). Pooled mixtures of cases by procedure were best fit by log-normal distributions. The noncentral-t-based log-normal tolerance limit, calculated per combination of procedure, surgeon, and facility, attained nominal 95% coverage in every configuration. Pooled Weibull and pooled nonparametric limits failed often (coverage 70.9%-79.2% and 62.9%-83.8%). The nonparametric method with all claim data attained 95.4%-97.1% coverage but was unavailable for 85% of surgeons at the realistic condition of unequal sample sizes, median n = 10. Applying the exact log-normal-based tolerance limits on 90 th percentiles functionally achieved percentiles ranging from the 92.1-97.4 th, with resulting payment satisfaction rates of 97.9%-100%. The per-surgeon log-normal 95% upper confidence limit for the 90 th percentile on log-transformed durations was the only valid method computable at realistic sample sizes. Applying those actuarially valid tolerance limits would pay ≈99.4% of historical case-time in full, thus functionally equivalent to retaining no paid time limit.

papers.abstract: The 2025 UK Code of Practice revised adult death determination using neurological criteria, including requirements for temperature, apnoea testing, and other aspects of assessment. National audit data describe how often testing occurs and record reasons for non-testing, but do not establish the consistency, quality, or physiological consequences of individual assessments. Testing rates were declining before the revised Code, precluding simple attribution of that decline to its introduction. We propose prospective patient-level evaluation from a predefined clinical screening trigger through assessment to confirmation of death, identification of persisting brainstem function, circulatory death before completion or after withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment, or continued treatment. A proposed dataset combines assessment timelines, individual prerequisites, test results, successive barriers, physiological events, and clinician experience. These findings should distinguish inconsistent interpretation from difficulties arising despite correct implementation and identify priorities for clarification, training, or focused evidence review.

papers.abstract: General anaesthesia for Caesarean delivery is increasingly used as a quality indicator, but general anaesthesia rates alone are not measures of quality. The multinational anaesthesia practice for Caesarean delivery snapshot study demonstrates variation in general anaesthesia use across European centres, emphasising the need to interpret these rates within the systems in which anaesthetic decisions occur. We propose an interpretation framework based on three domains: access to appropriate neuraxial care, reliability of neuraxial techniques and rescue pathways, and patient experience. The rates of general anaesthesia for Caesarean delivery should prompt investigation of system capacity rather than serve as verdicts on quality or safety.

papers.abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) measures cortical hemodynamics, yet its ability to characterize anesthesia-related functional changes remains unclear. This exploratory secondary analysis used prospectively collected data from 120 female patients undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery under propofol or sevoflurane anesthesia (60 per group). Twenty-channel prefrontal fNIRS recordings covered wakefulness, induction, and maintenance. Deoxygenated hemoglobin-derived amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF), functional connectivity (FC), network topology, and within- and cross-state FC similarity were assessed. Support vector machine, logistic regression, and random forest classifiers assessed discrimination between states. During induction, ALFF increased by 89.8% to 202.2% with propofol and 75.2% to 242.0% with sevoflurane across five prefrontal regions (all P < 0.001). During maintenance, mean ALFF was below awake levels, with significant reductions of 20.0% to 40.1% in three regions under sevoflurane (all P ≤ 0.019). Induction-related FC changes were limited and regionally heterogeneous. Regional FC, modularity, and global efficiency showed no significant maintenance-versus-awake differences in either group. Within-state between-subject FC similarity was significantly higher during maintenance than during wakefulness only with sevoflurane (mean difference [MD], 0.110; 95% CI, 0.054 to 0.169; P < 0.001). Cross-state between-subject FC similarity was higher for awake-maintenance than awake-induction comparisons with propofol (MD, 0.072; 95% CI, 0.055 to 0.090) and sevoflurane (MD, 0.144; 95% CI, 0.126 to 0.161; both P < 0.001). Support vector machine classification of induction versus wakefulness yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.83 (95% CI, 0.75 to 0.90) for propofol and 0.85 (95% CI, 0.78 to 0.91) for sevoflurane; maintenance-versus-awake AUCs were 0.67 (95% CI, 0.58 to 0.75) and 0.76 (95% CI, 0.68 to 0.85). Prefrontal fNIRS detected widespread induction-related hemodynamic changes, but the present connectivity measures provided limited discrimination between maintenance of anesthesia and wakefulness.

papers.abstract: Ultrasound-guided radial artery cannulation is common in pediatrics but technically challenging. While the ulnar artery is a potential alternative, its sonoanatomy relative to the radial artery is not well defined. This study aimed to compare the sonoanatomic characteristics of the radial and ulnar arteries in children, evaluating how age, weight, and wrist position (0°, 30°, and 45°) influence arterial dimensions and depth to identify the most favorable profile for cannulation. Ultrasound evaluation of the radial and ulnar arteries was performed at 0°, 30°, and 45° wrist extension in 180 anesthetized children aged 0-120 months using custom-made wooden blocks. Arterial dimensions and skin-to-artery distance were evaluated overall and across age (≤ 24 vs. > 24 months) and weight (≤ 12 vs. > 12 kg) subgroups to identify optimal access conditions. Wrist extension angle did not significantly affect anteroposterior diameter (1.4 ± 0.3 mm, p = 0.078), but significantly influenced transverse arterial diameter (1.5-1.6 mm, p = 0.003) and skin-to-artery distance (2.4-2.8 mm at 30°, p < 0.001). The radial artery was widest at 0° (1.6 ± 1.0 mm), while the ulnar artery peaked at 30° (1.6 ± 0.4 mm). Skin-to-artery distance was minimized at 30° for both vessels. In children ≤ 12 kg, radial transverse diameter decreased paradoxically from 0° to 45° (1.6 ± 0.4 to 1.4 ± 0.3 mm, p = 0.013), while the ulnar artery was widest at 30° (1.5 ± 0.3 mm, p = 0.007). In infants ≤ 24 months, wrist angle did not significantly influence radial artery depth (p = 0.631, mean overall depth between 2.5-2.6 mm). A 30° wrist extension angle provides the most favorable sonoanatomic profile for both arteries. Although a larger vessel caliber may potentially facilitate cannulation, its clinical benefit remains uncertain as cannulation outcomes were not assessed. These findings support individualized ultrasound-guided assessment rather than a fixed positioning strategy.

papers.abstract: The prevalence of obesity is rising. Patients with obesity are increasingly exposed to anaesthesia, critical care, and perioperative pharmacotherapy. Obesity alters drug pharmacokinetics in a non-linear, drug-specific manner, so that simply scaling doses to total body weight (TBW) exposes patients to overdose or underdose. A recurring clinical question is therefore: which body weight descriptor should be used for which molecule? This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews. We synthesized pharmacokinetic evidence, recent meta-analyses, and French and European guidelines on dose adjustment in adults with obesity for five drug classes of anaesthesia and critical care: hypnotics, opioids, neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBA), perioperative antibiotics, and non-opioid analgesics. We summarised the recommended dosing weight for each molecule in a table and a figure. No single weight descriptor applies. Lipophilic induction agents (propofol), most opioids (alfentanil, fentanyl, sufentanil), and non-depolarising NMBA are best dosed on lean or ideal body weight, whereas succinylcholine, neuromuscular reversal, and aminoglycosides use total or adjusted body weight. Maintenance of hypnosis and pain management in the post-anaesthesia care unit are titrated to monitored effect. Cephalosporin-based antibiotic prophylaxis relies on fixed doses (e.g., cefazolin 2 g) up to high body mass index values due to their hydrophilic properties. Paracetamol and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs are given at standard doses and never scaled to TBW. Findings are consolidated in a single bedside reference table. Dosing in obesity must be molecule-specific, guided by the relevant weight descriptor and by intraoperative monitoring rather than by TBW alone.

papers.abstract: The prognostic performance of the Simplified Acute Physiology Score (SAPS) models has not been thoroughly investigated. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed SAPS mortality prediction metrics across diverse intensive care unit (ICU) populations worldwide. PubMed and Scopus were queried for external validations of SAPS in ICU settings. The "CHARMS" and "PROBAST" tools were applied for data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment, respectively. C-statistics and observed-to-expected ratios were summarised using random-effects models. Heterogeneity sources were explored using meta-regression. Evidence certainty was evaluated using the "GRADE" approach. PROSPERO registration CRD42023446721. Ninety studies (89 articles) were reviewed, totalling 565,994 ICU patients across 87 countries, and validating the SAPS II (n = 35), SAPS 3 global (n = 37), and/or SAPS 3 region-specific (n = 28) models. Endpoints were in-hospital (n = 70), in-ICU (n = 16), and/or 28/30-day mortality (n = 12). Nine studies performed recalibrations of SAPS II and 7 of SAPS 3. The meta-analyses provided high-certainty evidence of excellent discriminatory ability across all SAPS models in predicting in-hospital mortality, whereas data on unsatisfactory overall calibration were graded as low certainty. Successful recalibration was graded as high certainty for SAPS II and moderate certainty for SAPS 3. For ICU and 28/30-day mortality, the evidence was low to very low certainty for all SAPS models. Five decision curve analyses were conducted in three studies, all yielding positive net benefit across meaningful risk thresholds. SAPS models remain reliable as mortality risk-ranking tools in critical care. With adequate sample sizes, local recalibrations and dynamic updating of in-hospital mortality predictions are essential to ensure clinical utility. PROSPERO CRD42023446721.

papers.abstract: To update the evidence on neurological and respiratory predictors of extubation failure after acute brain injury and to compare the two families, as pre-specified. Five databases were searched through July 2026 for studies relating a predictor measured at or near extubation to extubation failure in ventilated adults with acute brain injury. Screening and extraction were done in duplicate; risk of bias was assessed using QUIPS. Adjusted estimates were pooled after harmonising outcome framing and predictor coding, restricting each pool to one scale and instrument, with random-effects (REML, Hartung-Knapp) and Bayesian hierarchical models. Certainty was assessed using GRADE. 98 studies (24 505 patients) yielded 415 predictor-outcome estimates; 194 carried a confidence interval, and 6 studies contributed to pooled adjusted estimates. Absent or weak cough was associated with failure (4 studies; OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.46-4.19; posterior median 2.55, 95% CrI 1.54-4.71, P(OR > 1) = 0.999; I² = 0%; moderate certainty), in line with the previous synthesis; in an illustrative projection at a 19% failure rate, about 30% versus 15%. Below-threshold motor GCS was associated with failure in two concordant studies (posterior median OR 5.99, 2.42-16.1; very low certainty). The pre-specified comparison between families could not be validly estimated from published data. An absent or weak cough at extubation is the best-supported single bedside predictor of failure after acute brain injury and should be assessed with secretions, swallowing and consciousness. Fewer than one in ten eligible studies are poolable, mainly for remediable reporting reasons; a minimum reporting set is proposed. PROSPERO CRD420261442541 (submitted 6 July 2026; registered 2 September 2026). Protocol v2.3 was prepared before the searches; the PROSPERO amendment and all deviations are listed in Supplementary Table S1. PRISMA 2020 [1].

papers.abstract: Prophylactic norepinephrine infusion has gained increasing attention to prevent intraoperative hypotension during major non-cardiac surgery, but its effect on haemodynamic stability, tissue perfusion, fluid administration, and postoperative outcomes remains uncertain. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched through May 9, 2026 for randomised trials comparing prophylactic norepinephrine with standard reactive management. Outcomes included change in serum lactate, haemodynamic measures, fluid administration, and postoperative outcomes, including complications and mortality. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, respectively. Sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were performed. Eleven trials (1688 patients) were included. Prophylactic norepinephrine was associated with a lower rise in lactate (mean difference (MD) -0.13 mmol/L, 95% CI -0.25 to -0.01; P = 0.03; I²=67.2%), higher post-induction mean arterial pressure (MD 10.79 mmHg, 95% CI 5.53 to 16.04; P < 0.01; I²=95.3%), higher postoperative mean arterial pressure (MD 2.78 mmHg, 95% CI 0.63 to 4.92; P = 0.01; I²=69.8%). Prophylactic norepinephrine use was associated with lower crystalloid administration (MD-548.22 mL, 95% CI -1087.16 to -9.28, P = 0.05, I²=99%) although substantial heterogeneity and protocol-driven differences limit interpretation. Exploratory analyses suggested lower incidences of myocardial infarction (RR 0.25, 95% CI 0.06-0.98), pneumonia (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.36-0.95), and 30 day-surgical site infection (RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.41-0.97). No statistically significant differences were demonstrated for acute kidney injury, atelectasis, length of stay, or mortality. Certainty of evidence was low for most outcomes. TSA indicated insufficient evidence to establish a definitive treatment effect. Prophylactic norepinephrine was associated with a statistically significant but small reduction in intraoperative lactate rise, higher post-induction and post-operative mean arterial pressures. Postoperative complication findings remain exploratory and require confirmation in adequately powered randomised trials. PROSPERO (CRD420261345140).

papers.abstract: Observational studies have suggested that monitored anesthesia care (MAC) improves hospital throughput in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), though these findings largely reflect earlier practice patterns with longer hospitalizations, evolving care pathways, and limitations inherent to retrospective designs. We conducted a single-center, prospective randomized controlled trial of 170 patients undergoing elective transfemoral TAVR. Patients were randomized 1:1 to MAC or general endotracheal anesthesia (GETA) with intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography. The primary outcomes were hospital length of stay (LOS), 30-day mortality, and intensive care unit (ICU) admission. The secondary outcome was paravalvular regurgitation (PVR). Other prospectively tracked perioperative efficiency metrics included procedure time and operating room time. There was no significant difference in hospital LOS between the two groups (median difference in LOS, MAC vs GETA: 0.02 days (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.09 to 0.15 days); P = 0.631). There were no 30-day deaths in either group. ICU admission rates (P = 0.634) were similar between arms. No significant differences were observed in PVR rates (P = 0.934), procedure time (P = 0.142), or operating room time (P = 0.439). In a modern TAVR program, anesthetic technique did not influence hospital LOS or other clinical endpoints during the study. These findings suggest that the efficiency differences previously associated with MAC may not persist in current TAVR practice. Anesthetic choice can be individualized without substantially altering hospital throughput in similar practice settings.

papers.abstract: Regional analgesia is recommended for rib fractures, but utilization remains low. The extent to which hospital-level factors drive utilization and influence patient outcomes is unclear. This study's objective was to evaluate associations between hospital characteristics and regional analgesia receipt and outcomes. Retrospective cohort study using the Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS) of adult hospitalizations (>18 years) between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2022 with rib fractures. Exposures included hospital bed-size, ownership, teaching status and geographic region. Primary outcome was regional analgesia receipt. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and tracheostomy. 250,630 hospitalizations met inclusion criteria, of which 7,179 (2.9%) received regional analgesia. After adjustment, 23.9% of variation in utilization was attributable to between-hospital differences. Greater utilization was associated with large hospital bed-size (odds ratio [OR] 2.08; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.80-2.39), urban teaching-status (OR 1.39; 95% CI, 1.19-1.62), higher income-quartile (OR 1.21; 95% CI, 1.10-1.33), and private insurance (OR 1.24; 95% CI, 1.14-1.35). Lower odds were observed in private nonprofit (OR 0.75; 95% CI, 0.65-0.86) and for-profit hospitals (OR 0.42; 95% CI, 0.34-0.53) compared with government hospitals. Regional analgesia utilization varied geographically, with the highest utilization in New England. Private insurance, White race, highest income quartile, government ownership and urban teaching status were also associated with earlier receipt of regional anesthesia. Disparities by insurance and hospital characteristics either persisted or widened from 2016 to 2022.Regional analgesia was associated with lower mortality (OR, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.42-0.64) and tracheostomy (OR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.36-0.63) in multivariable analysis. In instrumental variable analysis with leave-one-out hospital-year regional analgesia rate as the instrument, these associations were attenuated. Regional analgesia remains infrequently utilized for rib fractures, with marked variation across hospitals. Access and outcomes appear to depend substantially on where patients receive care. Understanding the institutional and provider-level factors underlying this variation represents an important target for future quality-improvement and implementation efforts.
